analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between initiating moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and reduced risks of mortality and liver-related events in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Using the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database, the researchers followed 318,131 physically inactive adults with CHB over a median of 7.9 years. They found that MVPA initiation was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), reduced liver-related events (subHR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and a modest decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared to those who remained inactive. The associations were stronger in specific subgroups, including older adults, women, and untreated participants. The study highlights the potential public health significance of promoting physical activity in CHB patients, though it does not provide direct causal evidence.

title: Renal Safety and Antiviral Effectiveness of Tenofovir Alafenamide Versus Entecavir in Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B and Chronic Kidney Disease: A Real-World Cohort Study.
abstract: Real-world data on tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), especially in patients with advanced renal impairment, are scarce. We evaluated its renal safety and antiviral effectiveness versus entecavir (ETV) in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD). In this retrospective single-centre study, CHB patients with pre-existing CKD treated with TAF or ETV were included. The primary outcome was change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over 48 weeks. Secondary outcomes included virological, biochemical and metabolic responses. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed by CKD stage and dialysis status. Among 54 patients (35 TAF, 19 ETV), renal function remained stable in both groups. eGFR change from baseline to week 48 was not significantly different between the TAF and ETV groups (1.56 ± 8.14 vs. -0.53 ± 9.78 mL/min/1.73 m2; Δchange, 2.09; 95% CI, -0.35 to 7.68; p = 0.46). Both groups achieved sustained viral suppression, with no significant difference in undetectable HBV DNA in week-48. HBsAg reduction was greater with TAF than with ETV (-0.36 ± 0.42 vs. 0.02 ± 0.34 log10 IU/mL; p = 0.01). Exploratory analyses in patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, TAF showed effective viral suppression and renal safety regardless of dialysis status. Metabolic parameters remained stable, without complex dose adjustments. TAF was safe and effective in CHB patients with CKD, including those with advanced renal impairment. Its renal safety and antiviral effectiveness did not differ significantly from those of ETV, with the practical advantage of fixed dosing without complex adjustment.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the renal safety and antiviral effectiveness of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) compared to entecavir (ETV) in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD). A retrospective single-centre cohort study was conducted, including 54 patients (35 on TAF and 19 on ETV). The primary outcome was the change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over 48 weeks, while secondary outcomes included virological, biochemical, and metabolic responses. The results showed that renal function remained stable in both groups, with no significant difference in eGFR change between TAF and ETV. Both groups achieved sustained viral suppression, with no significant difference in undetectable HBV DNA at week 48. However, HBsAg reduction was greater with TAF than with ETV. Exploratory subgroup analyses indicated that TAF was effective and safe in patients with advanced renal impairment. The study highlights the potential of TAF as a treatment option for CHB patients with CKD, offering the advantage of fixed dosing without complex adjustments. The evidence is limited by the study's retrospective design and small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

abstract_zh: 关于替诺福韦艾拉酚胺(TAF)的现实世界数据,尤其是在肾功能严重受损的患者中,仍然非常有限。我们评估了TAF与恩替卡韦(ETV)在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)合并已有慢性肾脏病(CKD)患者中的肾脏安全性及有效性。本研究为一项回顾性单中心研究,纳入了接受TAF或ETV治疗的CHB合并已有CKD的患者。主要结局是48周内估算肾小球滤过率(eGFR)的变化。次要结局包括病毒学、生化和代谢反应。通过CKD阶段和透析状态进行了探索性亚组分析。在54名患者(35名接受TAF治疗,19名接受ETV治疗)中,两个组的肾功能均保持稳定。从基线到第48周,TAF组与ETV组的eGFR变化无显著差异(1.56 ± 8.14 vs. -0.53 ± 9.78 mL/min/1.73 m2;变化差值,2.09;95%置信区间,-0.35至7.68;p = 0.46)。两个组均实现了持续病毒抑制,第48周时检测不到HBV DNA无显著差异。TAF组的HBsAg下降幅度大于ETV组(-0.36 ± 0.42 vs. 0.02 ± 0.34 log10 IU/mL;p = 0.01)。在eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2的患者中,无论是否接受透析,TAF均表现出有效的病毒抑制和肾脏安全性。代谢参数保持稳定,无需复杂的剂量调整。TAF在CKD合并CHB患者中是安全且有效的,包括那些肾功能严重受损的患者。其肾脏安全性和有效性与ETV相比无显著差异,且具有固定剂量无需复杂调整的实用性优势。

title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy
abstract: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

title: Hepatitis B Vaccination Coverage and Factors Associated with Vaccine Uptake Among Dental Healthcare Workers in Shimonoseki, Japan
abstract: Background/Objectives: Dental healthcare workers (DHWs) are at high risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection due to occupational exposure. Although hepatitis B (HB) vaccination is recommended in Japan, vaccination coverage and factors associated with vaccine uptake remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify HB vaccination coverage, identify factors associated with vaccine uptake, and explore reasons for non-vaccination among DHWs in Shimonoseki, Japan. Methods: A cross-sectional web-based survey was conducted among 470 DHWs affiliated with the Shimonoseki Dental Association. Data on demographics, HBV/hepatitis C virus (HCV) testing, needlestick injuries, vaccination status, and reasons for non-vaccination were collected. Exploratory unadjusted group differences were analyzed using Chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Results: Of the 470 DHWs invited, 66 participated (response rate, 14.0%). Among respondents, 50.0% had a history of HB vaccination; however, only 22.7% had completed the three-dose series. Completion was significantly lower among dental staff than dentists (6.3% vs. Vaccination was associated with HBV-related education (p < 0.001), HBV/HCV testing history (HBV p < 0.001; HCV p < 0.001), and institutional policies (p = 0.0363), but not with needlestick injuries. Among the 27 unvaccinated respondents, the most frequently reported reason for non-vaccination was lack of personal recommendation. Conclusions: Among respondents, self-reported three-dose HB vaccination completion was low, particularly among dental staff. Vaccination status was associated with educational exposure, previous HBV/HCV testing, and reported workplace vaccination policies, whereas no association with self-reported needlestick injury history was observed.

title_zh: 日本下关牙科保健工作者乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 覆盖率和与 疫苗 吸收相关的因素
source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Dental healthcare workers (DHWs) are at high risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection due to occupational exposure. Although hepatitis B (HB) vaccination is recommended in Japan, vaccination coverage and factors associated with vaccine uptake remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify HB vaccination coverage, identify factors associated with vaccine uptake, and explore reasons for non-vaccination among DHWs in Shimonoseki, Japan. Methods: A cross-sectional web-based survey was conducted among 470 DHWs affiliated with the Shimonoseki Dental Association. Data on demographics, HBV/hepatitis C virus (HCV) testing, needlestick injuries, vaccination status, and reasons for non-vaccination were collected. Exploratory unadjusted group differences were analyzed using Chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Results: Of the 470 DHWs invited, 66 participated (response rate, 14.0%). Among respondents, 50.0% had a history of HB vaccination; however, only 22.7% had completed the three-dose series. Completion was significantly lower among dental staff than dentists (6.3% vs. Vaccination was associated with HBV-related education (p < 0.001), HBV/HCV testing history (HBV p < 0.001; HCV p < 0.001), and institutional policies (p = 0.0363), but not with needlestick injuries. Among the 27 unvaccinated respondents, the most frequently reported reason for non-vaccination was lack of personal recommendation. Conclusions: Among respondents, self-reported three-dose HB vaccination completion was low, particularly among dental staff. Vaccination status was associated with educational exposure, previous HBV/HCV testing, and reported workplace vaccination policies, whereas no association with self-reported needlestick injury history was observed.

title: Hepatitis B vaccination coverage among Indian dental students – Systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Objective To estimate the pooled estimates of hepatitis B vaccination (HBV) coverage among Indian dental students. Methods This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed (1946 onward), CINAHL (1937 onward), Dentistry and Oral Sciences Source (journal-specific coverage), Embase (1947 onward), Web of Science (1900 onward), and Scopus (1970 onward) till July 1st, 2025. Cross-sectional studies conducted among Indian dental students that reported HBV coverage and studies reported in English were included. The meta-analysis was performed via OpenMeta [Analyst] (random effects model with the restricted maximum likelihood method). Results A total of 24 studies that reported the HBV were included. (total sample: 8740 (age range: 18–27 years). The pooled estimate of complete HBV coverage was 53.9% (95%CI: 41.84, 65.97), with high heterogeneity (I 2 = 99.7). Monitoring of the antibody titer was reported in only 5 studies ( n = 504). Egger's regression revealed no publication bias (Z = 1.73; P = 0.08). Meta-regression revealed no significant effect of age or sex distribution on the estimates of HBV coverage. However, studies on clinical dental students reported higher estimates than studies that combined preclinical and clinical students (coefficient: 0.37; P < 0.01). Conclusion Approximately half of the dental students had not completed the three-dose HBV.

title: Serology-Anchored Comparison of Self-Reported Vaccination: Reported Hepatitis B Series Completion Exceeds Vaccine-Consistent Immunity in the Same Participants
abstract: A large secondary literature draws adult vaccination status from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), whose accuracy is rarely quantified alongside it. The objective of this article is to quantify that accuracy in the same participants, because its size and direction decide whether these items can support a coverage claim. The methods we used pooled ten NHANES cycles (1999–2018, adults ≥ 20 years; analytic n 13,992–48,959 by vaccine) and compared self-reported, completed-series uptake with a within-person biological reference. That reference exists for hepatitis B in 2015–2016 only and does not validate the hepatitis A or human papillomavirus (HPV) estimates. Our results are that among the 4473 respondents with both measures, self-reported vaccination rates (33.5%, 95% CI: 30.5–36.5%) stood 10.9 percentage points (7.5–14.3) above vaccine-consistent serology (22.6%, 19.9–25.2%), a ratio of 1.48 (1.30–1.67). They disagreed in both directions, 845 reporting the series without the serologic profile and 294 carrying the profile without reporting it, so the difference is not a measure of over-reporting. Tested directly, it was a near-constant multiple across sex, age, and race. Published National Health Interview Survey coverage, matched on dose definition, population, and year, gave ratios up to 3.00. Four adjusted estimators placed the effect of a usual source of care at 5.7–6.5 percentage points for hepatitis B and 2.5–3.2 for HPV, three excluding zero and the causal forest’s wider interval covering it. The conclusions drawn are that the two measures are not interchangeable and that NHANES figures should be read as reported uptake, not coverage surveillance.

title: Hepatitis B and C Screening Coverage among High-risk Populations in Saudi Arabia: A National Analysis of Surveillance Data and Alignment with the World Health Organization Viral Hepatitis Elimination Targets (2016–2023)
abstract: Abstract Background: Viral hepatitis B and C represent major global public health challenges, collectively responsible for approximately 1.1 million deaths annually. Saudi Arabia has historically demonstrated endemic hepatitis B transmission and carries a significant hepatitis C burden, yet comprehensive analyses of screening coverage among high-risk populations remain limited. Objectives: The objectives of the study were to characterize hepatitis B and C screening coverage patterns among high-risk populations in Saudi Arabia and evaluate alignment with the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Health Sector Strategy (GHSS) targets for viral hepatitis elimination by 2030. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed secondary data from the WHO Global Health Observatory estimates, Saudi Ministry of Health surveillance reports, and published epidemiological surveys (2016–2023). Screening coverage was assessed among defined high-risk groups including healthcare workers, blood donors, prisoners, patients on hemodialysis, and pregnant women. Descriptive statistics, including 95% confidence intervals (CIs), characterized coverage patterns by population group, geographic region, and temporal trends. Comparative analysis assessed alignment with the WHO GHSS targets. Results: Overall hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing coverage among high-risk populations reached 74.3% (95% CI: 74.2–74.4) in 2023, while anti-hepatitis C virus (HCV) testing coverage reached 68.9% (95% CI: 68.8–69.0). Blood donor screening achieved near-universal coverage (99.8%, 95% CI: 99.79–99.81, for both HBsAg and anti-HCV). Healthcare worker screening demonstrated 81.4% (95% CI: 81.3–81.5) HBsAg and 76.2% (95% CI: 76.0–76.4) anti-HCV coverage. Hemodialysis patient screening reached 94.7% (95% CI: 94.4–95.0) for HBsAg. Antenatal screening for HBsAg achieved 89.3% (95% CI: 89.2–89.4) nationally. However, prisoner screening remained lowest at 41.2% (95% CI: 40.8–41.6) for HBsAg and 38.7% (95% CI: 38.4–39.0) for anti-HCV. Regional disparities persisted, with border regions demonstrating 15–22 percentage point gaps below national averages. Temporal analysis revealed a modest improvement from 61.4% (95% CI: 61.3–61.5) in 2016 to 74.3% (95% CI: 74.2–74.4) in 2023 for HBsAg screening overall. Conclusions: Saudi Arabia has achieved strong screening coverage in clinical high-risk groups, but critical gaps persist among incarcerated populations and in border regions. Targeted expansion of screening programs, integration with primary health care, and strengthened linkage to care are essential to achieve the WHO 2030 viral hepatitis elimination targets.
journal: Journal of Nature and Science of Medicine

title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯高危人群乙型和丙型肝炎筛查覆盖率:监测 数据的全国分析以及与世界卫生组织病毒性肝炎消除目标(2016-2023 年)的一致性
source_body_en: Abstract Background: Viral hepatitis B and C represent major global public health challenges, collectively responsible for approximately 1.1 million deaths annually. Saudi Arabia has historically demonstrated endemic hepatitis B transmission and carries a significant hepatitis C burden, yet comprehensive analyses of screening coverage among high-risk populations remain limited. Objectives: The objectives of the study were to characterize hepatitis B and C screening coverage patterns among high-risk populations in Saudi Arabia and evaluate alignment with the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Health Sector Strategy (GHSS) targets for viral hepatitis elimination by 2030. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed secondary data from the WHO Global Health Observatory estimates, Saudi Ministry of Health surveillance reports, and published epidemiological surveys (2016–2023). Screening coverage was assessed among defined high-risk groups including healthcare workers, blood donors, prisoners, patients on hemodialysis, and pregnant women. Descriptive statistics, including 95% confidence intervals (CIs), characterized coverage patterns by population group, geographic region, and temporal trends. Comparative analysis assessed alignment with the WHO GHSS targets. Results: Overall hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing coverage among high-risk populations reached 74.3% (95% CI: 74.2–74.4) in 2023, while anti-hepatitis C virus (HCV) testing coverage reached 68.9% (95% CI: 68.8–69.0). Blood donor screening achieved near-universal coverage (99.8%, 95% CI: 99.79–99.81, for both HBsAg and anti-HCV). Healthcare worker screening demonstrated 81.4% (95% CI: 81.3–81.5) HBsAg and 76.2% (95% CI: 76.0–76.4) anti-HCV coverage. Hemodialysis patient screening reached 94.7% (95% CI: 94.4–95.0) for HBsAg. Antenatal screening for HBsAg achieved 89.3% (95% CI: 89.2–89.4) nationally. However, prisoner screening remained lowest at 41.2% (95% CI: 40.8–41.6) for HBsAg and 38.7% (95% CI: 38.4–39.0) for anti-HCV. Regional disparities persisted, with border regions demonstrating 15–22 percentage point gaps below national averages. Temporal analysis revealed a modest improvement from 61.4% (95% CI: 61.3–61.5) in 2016 to 74.3% (95% CI: 74.2–74.4) in 2023 for HBsAg screening overall. Conclusions: Saudi Arabia has achieved strong screening coverage in clinical high-risk groups, but critical gaps persist among incarcerated populations and in border regions. Targeted expansion of screening programs, integration with primary health care, and strengthened linkage to care are essential to achieve the WHO 2030 viral hepatitis elimination targets.

title: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen and Hepatitis D Antibody Positivity among Inmates of Jos Correctional Centre, Plateau State, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) share transmission pathways, and ongoing HDV replication requires HBV surface antigen. Evidence from correctional facilities in Nigeria remains limited. This study assessed hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HDV antibody positivity among inmates of Jos Correctional Centre. Methods: In a cross-sectional serological survey, plasma samples from 235 incarcerated participants was tested for HBsAg using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). HBsAg-reactive samples were subsequently tested for anti-HDV antibodies by ELISA. Descriptive frequencies and Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; Fisher’s exact test was used for selected sex- and exposure-stratified HBsAg comparisons. Results: HBsAg was detected in 43 of 235 participants (18.3%; 95% CI: 13.9–23.7%). Five of the 43 HBsAg-positive participants were anti-HDV positive (11.6%; 95% CI: 5.1–24.5%). HBsAg positivity was 42/227 (18.5%) among men and 1/8 (12.5%) among women (Fisher’s exact p = 1.00). Anti-HDV positivity occurred in five men and no women; only one HBsAg-positive woman was screened for anti-HDV. Small subgroup counts precluded reliable risk-factor inference. Conclusion: HBsAg and anti-HDV antibody positivity were observed in this correctional population. The findings support access to HBV screening, vaccination of susceptible individuals, HDV testing after HBsAg detection, and linkage to clinical assessment. Anti-HDV positivity alone does not establish active HDV infection.

title_zh: 尼日利亚高原州乔斯惩教中心囚犯的乙型肝炎表面抗原和丁型肝炎抗体阳性
source_body_en: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) share transmission pathways, and ongoing HDV replication requires HBV surface antigen. Evidence from correctional facilities in Nigeria remains limited. This study assessed hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HDV antibody positivity among inmates of Jos Correctional Centre. Methods: In a cross-sectional serological survey, plasma samples from 235 incarcerated participants was tested for HBsAg using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). HBsAg-reactive samples were subsequently tested for anti-HDV antibodies by ELISA. Descriptive frequencies and Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; Fisher’s exact test was used for selected sex- and exposure-stratified HBsAg comparisons. Results: HBsAg was detected in 43 of 235 participants (18.3%; 95% CI: 13.9–23.7%). Five of the 43 HBsAg-positive participants were anti-HDV positive (11.6%; 95% CI: 5.1–24.5%). HBsAg positivity was 42/227 (18.5%) among men and 1/8 (12.5%) among women (Fisher’s exact p = 1.00). Anti-HDV positivity occurred in five men and no women; only one HBsAg-positive woman was screened for anti-HDV. Small subgroup counts precluded reliable risk-factor inference. Conclusion: HBsAg and anti-HDV antibody positivity were observed in this correctional population. The findings support access to HBV screening, vaccination of susceptible individuals, HDV testing after HBsAg detection, and linkage to clinical assessment. Anti-HDV positivity alone does not establish active HDV infection.

title: Negatively Impacting Factors Against Effective Hepatitis B Vaccination
abstract: Introduction : Infection by the Hepatitis B virus is one of the greatest global public health issues. One study revealed that the world is facing about 3.61% of the overall HBV infection burden, with significant variation across countries. This study explores the negatively influencing factors that are hampering the effective Hepatitis-B vaccination. Methods: A review of the published studies that were written on the factors that hamper successful hepatitis B vaccination was conducted using the Google Scholar search engine. A total of 26 journal articles on negatively influencing factors of hepatitis B vaccination were studied, and the most relevant items during the last 10 years were identified and analyzed. Results: Overall, 18 barriers have been identified that hinder the effective uptake of hepatitis B vaccines. Those are lack of appropriate awareness and knowledge about Hepatitis B viral vaccination was identified as by far the highest factor and was 69% (18), simultaneiously, not having adequate education among parents is mentioned in more than 41% (11) of studies, followed by superstition and false perception or belief regarding vaccination as well as cultural barriers are also mentioned by 36% (9) of studies. On the other hand, the price of the vaccine and the unavailability of the vaccine are mentioned in 27% (7) of the reviewed articles. The fourth most mentioned barrier was lack of awareness among the health providers, along with inadequate knowledge of HBV among healthcare professionals, which was mentioned by 15% (4) of the reviewed studies. Issues differed from region to region. Conclusion: An appropriately planned and well-organized hepatitis B vaccination policy throughout the nation should be emphasized and prioritized to have adequate vaccine coverage after identifying the negatively influencing factors, and controlling those factors to eradicate the hepatitis B virus from the era. Medicine Today 2026, Vol.38 (2): 324-328

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver and antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) frequently coexists with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its association with antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB remains unclear. AIM To systematically evaluate the impact of MAFLD on antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB. METHODS This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched for studies published up to November 30, 2025. Meta-analyses were performed to assess associations between MAFLD and antiviral treatment responses or clinical outcomes. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate robustness. RESULTS Thirty-two studies were included, of which 20 evaluated antiviral treatment efficacy and 13 assessed clinical outcomes in patients with CHB and concomitant MAFLD (one study reported both treatment responses and clinical outcomes). MAFLD was associated with a higher rate of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at 48 weeks [odds ratio (OR) = 1.41, 95%CI: 1.28-1.55], although this association was attenuated at 96 weeks (OR = 1.44, 95%CI: 0.96-2.16). No significant association was observed between MAFLD and hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance at any time-point. MAFLD was consistently associated with lower rates of alanine aminotransferase normalization and hepatitis B virus DNA clearance throughout the treatment duration. MAFLD was associated with a significantly increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy (OR = 1.50, 95%CI: 1.01-2.24). Subgroup analyses according to the antiviral regimen revealed distinct patterns, partly explaining the heterogeneity in the overall analyses. Subgroup analyses suggested that the antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach partly explained the heterogeneity, particularly for hepatitis B virus DNA clearance and HCC. CONCLUSION MAFLD was associated with lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, particularly among patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and higher odds of HCC in patients with CHB, but not with hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance. These findings support metabolic risk assessment in CHB management and highlight the need for standardized MAFLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease definitions.

title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 中代谢功能障碍相关的脂肪肝和 抗病毒药物 反应:系统评价和荟萃分析
source_body_en: BACKGROUND Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) frequently coexists with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its association with antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB remains unclear. AIM To systematically evaluate the impact of MAFLD on antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB. METHODS This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched for studies published up to November 30, 2025. Meta-analyses were performed to assess associations between MAFLD and antiviral treatment responses or clinical outcomes. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate robustness. RESULTS Thirty-two studies were included, of which 20 evaluated antiviral treatment efficacy and 13 assessed clinical outcomes in patients with CHB and concomitant MAFLD (one study reported both treatment responses and clinical outcomes). MAFLD was associated with a higher rate of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at 48 weeks [odds ratio (OR) = 1.41, 95%CI: 1.28-1.55], although this association was attenuated at 96 weeks (OR = 1.44, 95%CI: 0.96-2.16). No significant association was observed between MAFLD and hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance at any time-point. MAFLD was consistently associated with lower rates of alanine aminotransferase normalization and hepatitis B virus DNA clearance throughout the treatment duration. MAFLD was associated with a significantly increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy (OR = 1.50, 95%CI: 1.01-2.24). Subgroup analyses according to the antiviral regimen revealed distinct patterns, partly explaining the heterogeneity in the overall analyses. Subgroup analyses suggested that the antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach partly explained the heterogeneity, particularly for hepatitis B virus DNA clearance and HCC. CONCLUSION MAFLD was associated with lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, particularly among patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and higher odds of HCC in patients with CHB, but not with hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance. These findings support metabolic risk assessment in CHB management and highlight the need for standardized MAFLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease definitions.

title: Discovery of XT1061, a HBV Capsid Assembly Modulator, as a Promising Therapeutic Candidate for Clinical Treatment of HBV Infection
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) persists as a major unresolved infectious disease. Patients typically require lifelong administration of nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) or interferons but seldom achieve functional cure. Recent studies indicate that HBV core assembly modulators (CAMs), when combined with NAs and interferons, can more effectively reduce HBsAg in plasma, thereby facilitating functional cure. In this research, we discovered compound 39 (designated XT1061) through structural optimization of previously reported GLP-26, which exhibited potent anti-HBV activity in vitro (EC50 = 1.0 ± 0.1 nM). In the murine AAV/HBV model, XT1061 induced rapid reduction of HBV DNA and sustained viral DNA clearance throughout treatment. Notably, Combination therapy of XT1061 with pradefovir mesylate (PDV) exhibited significantly enhanced efficacy compared with monotherapy. Further preclinical evaluation and Phase I clinical trials (NCT06280534) confirmed that XT1061 possesses favorable drug-like properties and low safety risks. Collectively, XT1061 represents a promising anti-HBV therapeutic candidate, providing a viable strategy for the clinical management of chronic HBV infection.

Recent studies indicate that HBV core assembly modulators (CAMs), when combined with NAs and interferons, can more effectively reduce HBsAg in plasma, thereby facilitating functional cure. In this research, we discovered compound 39 (designated XT1061) through structural optimization of previously reported GLP-26, which exhibited potent anti-HBV activity in vitro (EC50 = 1.0 ± 0.1 nM). In the murine AAV/HBV model, XT1061 induced rapid reduction of HBV DNA and sustained viral DNA clearance throughout treatment. Notably, Combination therapy of XT1061 with pradefovir mesylate (PDV) exhibited significantly enhanced efficacy compared with monotherapy. Further preclinical evaluation and Phase I clinical trials (NCT06280534) confirmed that XT1061 possesses favorable drug-like properties and low safety risks. Collectively, XT1061 represents a promising anti-HBV therapeutic candidate, providing a viable strategy for the clinical management of chronic HBV infection.

title: Hepatitis B and C infections and risk of age related macular degeneration in a nationwide Korean cohort
abstract: Abstract Evidence on viral hepatitis and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains limited, particularly from long-term prospective studies. We investigated whether hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are associated with the subsequent development of AMD in a nationwide Korean cohort. Using National Health Insurance Service data, we included 12,386,563 adults aged ≥ 40 years who underwent health examinations in 2009–2010 and were followed through 2023. HBV and HCV infections were identified using diagnostic codes. Incident AMD was classified as exudative using Rare Intractable Disease registration codes and as nonexudative using Korean Classification of Diseases codes. During follow-up, 388,652 participants developed incident AMD. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, HBV infection was associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05–1.32) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.60–1.76). HCV infection was also associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.27–1.86) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.27–1.57). Associations appeared stronger in women in sex-stratified analyses. HBV and HCV infections were associated with increased risks of both exudative and nonexudative AMD.

elements_zh.main_results: In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, HBV infection was associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05–1.32) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.60–1.76). analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are associated with the subsequent development of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in a nationwide Korean cohort. Abstract Evidence on viral hepatitis and AMD remains limited, particularly from long-term prospective studies.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A nationwide cohort study was conducted using National Health Insurance Service data, including 12,386,563 adults aged ≥ 40 years who underwent health examinations in 2009–2010 and were followed through 2023. During follow-up, 388,652 participants developed incident AMD.
analysis_en.methods: HBV and HCV infections were identified using diagnostic codes. Incident AMD was classified as exudative using Rare Intractable Disease registration codes and as nonexudative using Korean Classification of Diseases codes. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations.
analysis_en.main_results: In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, HBV infection was associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05–1.32) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.60–1.76). HCV infection was also associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.27–1.86) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.27–1.57).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that HBV and HCV infections are associated with increased risks of both exudative and nonexudative AMD. This is a novel observation linking viral hepatitis to AMD.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that viral hepatitis infections may contribute to the risk of AMD, which could inform future surveillance and prevention strategies for AMD in populations with high hepatitis prevalence.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on diagnostic codes for identifying infections and AMD, which may introduce misclassification bias. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

title_zh: 韩国全国范围内的乙型和丙型肝炎感染与年龄相关性黄斑变性的风险 队列研究
source_body_en: Abstract Evidence on viral hepatitis and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains limited, particularly from long-term prospective studies. We investigated whether hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are associated with the subsequent development of AMD in a nationwide Korean cohort. Using National Health Insurance Service data, we included 12,386,563 adults aged ≥ 40 years who underwent health examinations in 2009–2010 and were followed through 2023. HBV and HCV infections were identified using diagnostic codes. Incident AMD was classified as exudative using Rare Intractable Disease registration codes and as nonexudative using Korean Classification of Diseases codes. During follow-up, 388,652 participants developed incident AMD. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, HBV infection was associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05–1.32) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.60–1.76). HCV infection was also associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.27–1.86) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.27–1.57). Associations appeared stronger in women in sex-stratified analyses. HBV and HCV infections were associated with increased risks of both exudative and nonexudative AMD.

title: Prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) in Cte dIvoire
abstract: Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease.In Côte d'Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication.This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAgpositive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d'Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021.HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888-1122 and 313-485).Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years.HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%).Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43).This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors.HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia.Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates.These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection.Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa.
journal: International Journal of Genetics and Molecular Biology

title_original: Prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) in Cte dIvoire

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d'Ivoire, HDV is not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021 at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d'Ivoire (CNTSCI). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and the mean age was 37 ± 9 years.
analysis.methods: HDV RNA was detected by nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888-1122 and 313-485). HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%).
analysis.main_results: Among the 43 donors with available HBV DNA results, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity of 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data, not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of HDV screening in individuals with chronic HBV infection, particularly in settings where viral load data is available, and suggest the need for further research to better understand HDV prevalence and its implications for public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single study with limited generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg-positive blood donors in Côte d'Ivoire using nested RT-PCR. It found that 90.7% of donors with available HBV DNA results had HDV RNA positivity, with 100% positivity in those with undetectable HBV viral load. The study highlights the need for systematic HDV screening in individuals with chronic HBV infection, particularly in follow-up care settings. However, the findings are hypothesis-generating due to the convenience sample and limited generalizability, indicating moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 感染会加剧 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关的肝病。在科特迪瓦,丁型肝炎病毒并未在乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性的献血者中进行系统筛查,大多数地区的估计依赖于抗丁型肝炎病毒 血清学,这表明存在暴露,但不代表活跃复制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2021 年 3 月,科特迪瓦国家输血中心 (CNTSCI) 的献血者医疗随访中心 (CMSDS) 进行了一项基于非概率便利样本的横断面研究。在 51 名捐赠者中,75% 是男性 (n = 38),平均年龄为 37 ± 9 岁。
elements_zh.methods: HDV RNA 通过针对两个基因组区域(核苷酸 888-1122 和 313-485)的巢式逆转录聚合酶链式反应 (RT-PCR) 进行检测。43 名捐献者 (84%) 可获得 HBV DNA 结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 43 名可获得 HBV DNA 结果的捐献者中,可检测到 HBV 病毒血症的 HDV RNA 阳性率为 88.9% (32/36),而病毒载量无法检测到的捐献者则为 100% (7/7),总体阳性率为 90.7% (39/43)。该数字仅适用于具有可用病毒载量数据的捐赠者,而不是 51 名捐赠者的整个 队列研究。在接受富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 且 HBV 病毒血症受到抑制的捐赠者中也检测到了 HDV RNA。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果支持在慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染者的随访过程中进行更大规模的代表性研究和系统性丁型肝炎病毒筛查。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了丁型肝炎病毒筛查对慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染者的重要性,特别是在可获得病毒载量数据的情况下,并表明需要进一步研究以更好地了解丁型肝炎病毒 患病率 及其对公共卫生的影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 鉴于已经接受后续护理的捐赠者的方便样本,研究结果是假设生成而不是人口水平的估计。该证据是中等的,因为它基于一项具有有限普遍性的研究。

title: Chronic Hepatitis B and Steatotic Liver Disease: From Bidirectional Interaction to Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and steatotic liver disease (SLD) are among the most prevalent chronic liver diseases worldwide and increasingly coexist, particularly in regions where hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains endemic. Reported prevalence of hepatic steatosis in CHB varies widely, reflecting the diagnostic modality and population studied rather than a single underlying figure. Across series using liver biopsy, ultrasound or controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), hepatic steatosis in CHB is associated more consistently with host metabolic and genetic factors than with markers of viral replication. Hepatic steatosis is repeatedly associated with lower serum HBV DNA, lower quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), lower hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg) positivity and a higher probability of HBsAg seroclearance. These virological associations do not consistently predict long-term liver outcomes, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists after HBsAg seroclearance. Studies using hepatic steatosis as the exposure report inconsistent findings for HCC, with adjusted estimates ranging from inverse to strongly positive. Metabolic dysfunction shows a more consistent association with HCC, particularly diabetes, obesity and multiple concurrent cardiometabolic risk factors, and this association persists in virologically suppressed patients and after HBsAg seroclearance. Hepatic steatosis, metabolic dysfunction, steatohepatitis and fibrosis should therefore be assessed as distinct prognostic variables rather than as a single entity, with implications for HCC risk stratification and surveillance in CHB.

abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 和脂肪肝病 (SLD) 是全球最常见的慢性肝病之一,并且越来越多地共存,特别是在 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然流行的地区。报道的慢性乙型肝炎肝脂肪变性的 患病率 差异很大,反映了诊断方式和研究的人群,而不是单一的基础数据。在使用肝活检、超声或受控衰减参数 (CAP) 的系列研究中,CHB 中的肝脂肪变性与 宿主 代谢和遗传因素的相关性比与病毒复制标志物的相关性更一致。肝脂肪变性反复与较低的血清 HBV DNA、较低的乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 定量、较低的乙型肝炎包膜抗原 (HBeAg) 阳性率以及较高的 HBsAg 血清清除概率相关。这些病毒学关联并不能一致地预测长期肝脏结果,并且 HBsAg 血清清除后肝细胞癌 (HCC) 风险仍然存在。使用肝脂肪变性作为暴露的研究报告了 HCC 的不一致结果,调整后的估计范围从反向到强正。代谢功能障碍与 HCC 存在更一致的关联,特别是糖尿病、肥胖和多种并发心脏代谢危险因素,并且这种关联在病毒学抑制的患者和 HBsAg 血清清除后持续存在。因此,肝脂肪变性、代谢功能障碍、脂肪性肝炎和纤维化应作为不同的预后变量而不是作为单一实体进行评估,这对 HCC 风险分层和 CHB 中的 监测 具有影响。

title: CD161-lectin-like transcript 1 axis beyond programmed cell death protein 1 in hepatitis B virus-associated hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated hepatocellular carcinoma develops in a chronically inflamed, tolerogenic liver microenvironment. In this setting, T-cell dysfunction limits the efficacy of programmed death-1 (PD-1) blockade. Emerging evidence from Liu et al published in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology suggests that CD161 may represent an additional inhibitory axis within exhausted CD8+ T cells that is not fully captured by the PD-1/ programmed death ligand-1 pathway. In their study, CD161+CD8+ T cells were enriched in tumor tissue, and CD161 expression persisted even as PD-1+ compartments contracted after PD-1 inhibition, suggesting that CD161-mediated restraint may remain active under therapeutic pressure. Mechanistically, sustained engagement of the CD161-lectin-like transcript 1 interaction may impair T-cell effector function and contribute to adaptive immune resistance in the HBV-infected liver. These findings highlight the importance of protein-level assessment of CD161 and parallel evaluation with PD-1 to accurately characterize immune inhibition. Key knowledge gaps include the cellular source of lectin-like transcript 1 within the tumor microenvironment, the influence of ongoing HBV virological activity on CD161+ T-cell subsets, and the identification of clinically meaningful progression endpoints. In this editorial, we place these findings in mechanistic and translational context, highlighting the potential role of the CD161-lectin-like transcript 1 axis as a complementary pathway of immune resistance beyond PD-1 blockade. Collectively, the current evidence supports a cautious, hypothesis-driven translational strategy to evaluate combined modulation of the CD161 and PD-1 axes in carefully selected patients with HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 相关肝细胞癌中 CD161 凝集素样转录物 1 轴超出程序性细胞死亡蛋白 1
source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated hepatocellular carcinoma develops in a chronically inflamed, tolerogenic liver microenvironment. In this setting, T-cell dysfunction limits the efficacy of programmed death-1 (PD-1) blockade. Emerging evidence from Liu et al published in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology suggests that CD161 may represent an additional inhibitory axis within exhausted CD8+ T cells that is not fully captured by the PD-1/ programmed death ligand-1 pathway. In their study, CD161+CD8+ T cells were enriched in tumor tissue, and CD161 expression persisted even as PD-1+ compartments contracted after PD-1 inhibition, suggesting that CD161-mediated restraint may remain active under therapeutic pressure. Mechanistically, sustained engagement of the CD161-lectin-like transcript 1 interaction may impair T-cell effector function and contribute to adaptive immune resistance in the HBV-infected liver. These findings highlight the importance of protein-level assessment of CD161 and parallel evaluation with PD-1 to accurately characterize immune inhibition. Key knowledge gaps include the cellular source of lectin-like transcript 1 within the tumor microenvironment, the influence of ongoing HBV virological activity on CD161+ T-cell subsets, and the identification of clinically meaningful progression endpoints. In this editorial, we place these findings in mechanistic and translational context, highlighting the potential role of the CD161-lectin-like transcript 1 axis as a complementary pathway of immune resistance beyond PD-1 blockade. Collectively, the current evidence supports a cautious, hypothesis-driven translational strategy to evaluate combined modulation of the CD161 and PD-1 axes in carefully selected patients with HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关肝细胞癌在慢性炎症、耐受性肝脏微环境中发生。在这种情况下,T 细胞功能障碍限制了程序性死亡 1 (PD-1) 阻断的功效。Liu 等人发表在《世界胃肠肿瘤学杂志》上的新证据表明,CD161 可能代表耗尽的 CD8+ T 细胞内的另一个抑制轴,该轴未被 PD-1/程序性死亡配体-1 通路完全捕获。在他们的研究中,CD161+CD8+T细胞在肿瘤组织中富集,即使PD-1+区室在PD-1抑制后收缩,CD161表达仍然持续,这表明CD161介导的抑制可能在治疗压力下保持活跃。从机制上讲,CD161-凝集素样转录物 1 相互作用的持续参与可能会损害 T 细胞效应器功能,并有助于 HBV 感染肝脏中的适应性免疫抵抗。这些发现强调了 CD161 蛋白质水平评估和 PD-1 平行评估对于准确表征免疫抑制的重要性。关键知识差距包括肿瘤微环境中凝集素样转录物 1 的细胞来源、持续的 HBV 病毒学活性对 CD161+ T 细胞亚群的影响,以及临床有意义的进展终点的识别。在这篇社论中,我们将这些发现置于机制和转化背景中,强调了 CD161 凝集素样转录物 1 轴作为 PD-1 阻断之外的免疫抵抗的补充途径的潜在作用。总的来说,当前的证据支持谨慎的、假设驱动的转化策略,以评估精心挑选的 HBV 相关肝细胞癌患者中 CD161 和 PD-1 轴的联合调节。

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

title_zh: 通过机器学习实现针对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝纤维化的个性化预测
source_body_en: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.
abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

title: Association of IL-10 (rs1800896) Gene Polymorphism and Serum IL-10 Levels with Chronic Hepatitis B Infection
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a main general validity threat. It evolves under the influence of various factors, including immunogenetic ones. This study assessed the correlation between the occurrence of interleukin 10 gene (IL10) polymorphisms and the development of these infections. This retrospective case control study 64 chronic HBV infections, 39 HBV clearance groups and 31 controls. "Tetra-primer ARMS-PCR" is a technique that used to study the single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) at IL10 promoter (-1082A>G; rs1800896). The IL-10 levels were determined in patients with chronic HBV infections, HBV clearance and control group by using an Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA). Based on allele polymorphism analysis, three genotypes were identified: AA (46.8 %), AG (43.7 %) and GG (9.3 %). The level of IL10 in HBV patients was significantly greater than that in other sets. In addition, these findings indicate that polymorphism may not affect initial infection but rather disease progression or disease immune response.
journal: Journal of Wasit for Science and Medicine

title: Translational Multiplexed Raman Pathological Imaging for Precise Diagnosis of HBV-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Multiplexed vibrational imaging holds great potential for tissue molecular analysis, yet fully standardized workflows suitable for routine clinical histopathology remain scarce. Herein, we report a clinically applicable methodology using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles (∼50 nm). This approach integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to achieve high-performance multiplexed Raman imaging of 5 protein markers in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues. Targeting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated HCC, our biomarker panel combines the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. We further reveal a clinically critical dissociation: several high-grade HBV-HCC specimens exhibit markedly elevated oncogenic markers with comparatively low HBx expression, consistent with antiviral therapy suppressing viral protein production without reversing tumor aggressiveness. Taking advantage of the ultranarrow, well-resolved signals generated by triple-bond tags within the biological silent region (1800−2800 cm−1), we achieve high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis. Unlike conventional pathological methods relying on morphological observation, clinical manifestations, or single-marker detection, this technique simultaneously evaluates viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, effectively reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles, and completes the entire assay within approximately 24 h. This study establishes a rapid and reliable histopathological platform that integrates pathogen identification and comprehensive cancer characterization, demonstrating substantial value for both cancer research and clinical diagnostics.

Herein, we report a clinically applicable methodology using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles (∼50 nm). This approach integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to achieve high-performance multiplexed Raman imaging of 5 protein markers in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues. Targeting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated HCC, our biomarker panel combines the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. We further reveal a clinically critical dissociation: several high-grade HBV-HCC specimens exhibit markedly elevated oncogenic markers with comparatively low HBx expression, consistent with antiviral therapy suppressing viral protein production without reversing tumor aggressiveness. Taking advantage of the ultranarrow, well-resolved signals generated by triple-bond tags within the biological silent region (1800−2800 cm−1), we achieve high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis. Unlike conventional pathological methods relying on morphological observation, clinical manifestations, or single-marker detection, this technique simultaneously evaluates viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, effectively reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles, and completes the entire assay within approximately 24 h. This study establishes a rapid and reliable histopathological platform that integrates pathogen identification and comprehensive cancer characterization, demonstrating substantial value for both cancer research and clinical diagnostics.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过开发一种临床适用的方法来精确检测 HBV 相关肝细胞癌的 诊断,从而解决常规临床组织病理学缺乏完全标准化工作流程的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究报告了一种临床适用的方法,使用单分散三键拉曼聚合物纳米颗粒(∼50 nm)实现肝细胞癌(HCC)组织中 5 种蛋白质标记物的高性能多重拉曼成像。
elements_zh.methods: 该技术集成了一步标记和单次扫描采集,可同时评估病毒病因、肿瘤进展和转移潜力,有效降低病毒和致癌谱不一致患者的错误分类风险,并在约 24 小时内完成整个检测。
elements_zh.main_results: 该方法针对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关 HCC,将病毒蛋白 HBx 与 4 个临床使用的指标相结合:AFP、GS、GPC3 和 CD34。它进一步揭示了临床上关键的分离:几个高级别 HBV-HCC 标本表现出显着升高的致癌标志物,而 HBx 表达相对较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这种方法通过利用生物沉默区域(1800−2800 cm−1)内三键标签产生的超窄、高分辨率信号来实现高保真空间绘图和定量分析,这是病原体识别和全面癌症表征的新颖整合。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现证明了对癌症研究和临床诊断的巨大价值,特别是在提高 诊断 对 HBV 相关肝细胞癌的准确性方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象证据,并且该方法在常规临床环境中的有效性尚未得到充分验证,因此可信度评估为中等。

title_zh: 转化多重拉曼病理成像对 HBV 相关肝细胞癌的精确 诊断

abstract_zh: 摘要:多重振动成像在组织分子分析方面具有巨大潜力,但适合常规临床组织病理学的完全标准化工作流程仍然很少。在此,我们报告了一种使用单分散三键拉曼聚合物纳米颗粒(∼50 nm)的临床适用方法。该方法集成了一步标记和单次扫描采集,可实现肝细胞癌 (HCC) 组织中 5 种蛋白质标记物的高性能多重拉曼成像。针对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关 HCC,我们的生物标志物组合将病毒蛋白 HBx 与 4 个临床使用的指标相结合:AFP、GS、GPC3 和 CD34。我们进一步揭示了临床上关键的分离:几个高级别 HBV-HCC 标本表现出显着升高的致癌标志物,而 HBx 表达相对较低,这与 抗病毒药物 疗法抑制病毒蛋白产生而不逆转肿瘤侵袭性一致。利用生物沉默区域(1800−2800 cm−1)内三键标签产生的超窄、高分辨率信号,我们实现了高保真空间映射和定量分析。与依赖形态学观察、临床表现或单标志物检测的传统病理方法不同,该技术同时评估病毒病原学、肿瘤进展和转移潜力,有效降低病毒和致癌谱不一致患者的错误分类风险,并在约24小时内完成整个检测。这项研究建立了一个快速、可靠的组织病理学平台,整合了病原体识别和全面的癌症表征,展示了对癌症研究和临床诊断的巨大价值。

title: Metabolomics reveals metabolite profiles associated with clinical cure of chronic HBV infection under different drug interventions
abstract: Objectives: To identify differential metabolites associated with complete cure in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with various regimens of entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Methods: The retrospective, case-control study was conducted at the Mudan People's Hospital of Heze, Shandong, China, and comprised samples from the institutional laboratory department of hepatitis B virus patients enrolled between June 2, 2021, and December 30, 2023. The patients were grouped based on the treatment protocol and the evidence of complete cure. Groups A and B comprised patients who were and were not clinically cured after receiving 48 weeks of sequential entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Group E patients received entecavir monotherapy for over 2 years without a clinical cure, and group W included untreated patients. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and metabolomics databases were utilised to identify differential metabolites and networks indicative of clinical cure. Data was analysed using the R language Ropls package. Results: Of the 50 patients, 13(26%) each were in Group A and Group B, while 12(24%) each were in Group E and Group W. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify differential metabolites associated with clinical cure in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Conducted at Mudan People's Hospital in China, it involved a retrospective case-control design with patients grouped based on treatment and cure status. Kaempferide and other metabolites showed significant fold-change values, suggesting their potential role in clinical cure. The results may help develop biomarkers for treatment monitoring. However, the study's retrospective nature and small sample size limit its generalisability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Pilot Model for Newly Diagnosed in-Hospital Bacterial and Fungal Infections in Decompensated Hepatitis B Cirrhosis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background and Aims: Recognizing infection risk during hospitalization is important in decompensated cirrhosis, although routine measurements may reflect infection already developing. We developed and internally validated an admission-time pilot model for newly diagnosed in-hospital bacterial or fungal infection in decompensated hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 150 patients admitted in 2023– 2025. Admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score (MELD) were fixed as predictors for the primary Firth/Jeffreys penalized logistic model. Complete-case analysis included 148 patients and 20 events. We refitted the fixed model in 1000 bootstrap samples, assessed calibration and discrimination, and examined early-event exclusions and an admission-only ridge model. The hospital-recorded procedure variable was excluded from prediction. Secondary analyses used Aalen–Johansen cumulative incidence, Fine–Gray regression and cause-specific Cox, with infection-free discharge and death as competing events. Results: Among 148 modeled patients, the NLR and MELD odds ratios were 1.073 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.025– 1.124) and 1.062 (95% CI, 1.002– 1.125). Apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.716 versus 0.633 for MELD alone. Optimism-corrected AUC was 0.700 (approximate 95% CI 0.566– 0.846), corrected Brier score was 0.103, and corrected calibration slope was 0.981 (approximate bootstrap interval 0.506– 1.646). AUCs after separate exclusions of infections recorded by hospital day 2 or day 3 were 0.750 and 0.731, respectively. Fine–Gray subdistribution hazard ratios were 1.069 (95% CI 1.042– 1.098) for NLR and 1.064 (1.021– 1.109) for MELD. Conclusion: This admission model showed modest discrimination with imprecise calibration. Retrospective ascertainment and limited validation preclude clinical use. Prospective external validation at a defined prediction time and horizon is needed before the model guides surveillance or treatment. Keywords: hepatitis B, decompensated cirrhosis, infection, prediction model, internal validation, nomogram

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a pilot model for predicting newly diagnosed in-hospital bacterial or fungal infections in patients with decompensated hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis. A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from 150 patients admitted between 2023 and 2025. The model incorporated admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) scores as predictors. Results showed modest discrimination with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.716, and imprecise calibration. The study concluded that the model requires prospective external validation before it can be used in clinical practice. The findings suggest that further research is needed to improve the model's accuracy and applicability for surveillance and treatment decisions in patients with HBV-related cirrhosis.

title: Epidemiology of Hepatitis B and C Viral Infections Among Tuberculosis Patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria
abstract: Tuberculosis patients coinfected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) may be particularly vulnerable to liver injury during treatment. Evidence on the burden and clinical implications of these infections in Ebonyi State remains limited. The aim of the study is to assess the epidemiology of Hepatitis B and C Viruses Infection among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to (i) determine the prevalence of HBV, HCV, and HBV/HCV co-infection among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, (ii) to identify common risk factors among co-infected TB-patients with viral hepatitis B and C in Ebonyi State. (iii) to determine the knowledge, attitude and practice of TB patients towards HBV and HCV infections. This study assessed HBV/HCV prevalence, risk factors, and patients’ knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP).
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: Pegylated interferon α-2b add-on to nucleos(t)ide analogues reduces hepatocellular carcinoma and decompensation in advanced fibrotic chronic hepatitis B
abstract: BACKGROUND The current therapeutic strategy of adding pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) is primarily aimed at achieving functional cure. However, its value in improving prognosis and the suitable candidates for this combination strategy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis remain to be further explored. AIM To evaluate the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. METHODS This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients diagnosed with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. Participants were divided into two groups: (1) Those receiving combination therapy (Peg-IFNα-2b add-on to ongoing NA treatment); and (2) Those receiving NA monotherapy. A 1:1 propensity score matching approach was applied to balance baseline characteristics between groups. In survival analysis, the outcomes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis were stratified by baseline clinical features and established HCC risk scores. RESULTS The analysis included 302 matched pairs, with a median follow-up duration of 220 weeks. Combination therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of developing HCC (hazard ratio = 0.22; 95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and decompensated cirrhosis (hazard ratio = 0.39; 95%CI: 0.20-0.77) than NA monotherapy. These benefits were particularly pronounced among patients classified as intermediate-to-high risk by validated HCC prediction models and in those with persistent biochemical abnormalities lasting > 12 months. CONCLUSION Add-on therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b to NAs is significantly associated with reduced HCC and decompensation in high-risk patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, supporting its use in this population.

AIM To evaluate the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. METHODS This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients diagnosed with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. Participants were divided into two groups: (1) Those receiving combination therapy (Peg-IFNα-2b add-on to ongoing NA treatment); and (2) Those receiving NA monotherapy. A 1:1 propensity score matching approach was applied to balance baseline characteristics between groups. In survival analysis, the outcomes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis were stratified by baseline clinical features and established HCC risk scores. RESULTS The analysis included 302 matched pairs, with a median follow-up duration of 220 weeks. Combination therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of developing HCC (hazard ratio = 0.22; 95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and decompensated cirrhosis (hazard ratio = 0.39; 95%CI: 0.20-0.77) than NA monotherapy. These benefits were particularly pronounced among patients classified as intermediate-to-high risk by validated HCC prediction models and in those with persistent biochemical abnormalities lasting > 12 months. CONCLUSION Add-on therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b to NAs is significantly associated with reduced HCC and decompensation in high-risk patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, supporting its use in this population.

title: Immune Response to Hepatitis B Vaccination According to National EPI Schedule among Children Below 2 Years
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus infection is a public health burden globally. We incorporate Hep-B vaccine in our EPI schedule. There is no comprehensive data regarding the immune response of the HBV vaccine at one year in our country. The study was done to assess the immune response among HBV vaccinated children at this age group. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at EPI outdoor of Chittagong Medical College Hospital from January to December, 2022. Blood sample from 375 vaccinated children were tested for Anti-HBs titre by ELISA technique in between 9 months to 15 months. Statistical analyses were performed with Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 23.0. Results: This study shows that older children and male tend to have better immune responses after vaccination and malnutrition is a significant risk factor for low antibody titers. This study also shows that 79.2% of children had satisfactory or high levels of anti-HBs antibodies (≥10 mIU/mL). However, 20.8% of children had low antibody titers ( <10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection. Conclusion: Most children vaccinated under the current EPI schedule develop protective immunity against hepatitis B; a small proportion remain vulnerable due to inadequate seroconversion. Chatt Maa Shi Hosp Med Coll J; Vol.25 (2); July 2026; Page 10-15
journal: Chattagram Maa-O-Shishu Hospital Medical College Journal

title: Intrinsic replication advantage of a Hepatitis B Virus genotype C strain is independent of the basal core promoter A1762T/G1764A mutation
abstract: This study aimed to isolate and characterize individual hepatitis B virus (HBV) strains from a patient co-infected with genotype B and C, and to directly compare their intrinsic replication capacities. HBV DNA was isolated from a chronic hepatitis B patient. Genotypes were determined by genotype-specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and full-length genomes were cloned. Two clones representing subgenotype B2 (c17) and C1 (c21) were selected, sequenced and transfected into HepG2 cells. Viral replication was assessed via Southern blot and quantitative PCR. The role of the common Adenine (A)1762Thymine (T/)Guanine (G)1764A mutation in the C1 clone was investigated by site-directed mutagenesis. As a result, the genotype C1 clone exhibited significantly higher replication capacity than the B2 clone. Counterintuitively, reverting the A1762T/G1764A mutation in the C1 clone to wild-type further enhanced its replication, indicating this mutation was not the primary driver of its high replicative fitness. In conclusion, HBV genotype C1 possesses a greater inherent replication capacity than B2, independent of the classic basal core promoter (BCP) mutation, providing a virological explanation for its association with severe disease outcomes in co-infection.

Two clones representing subgenotype B2 (c17) and C1 (c21) were selected, sequenced and transfected into HepG2 cells. Viral replication was assessed via Southern blot and quantitative PCR. The role of the common Adenine (A)1762Thymine (T/)Guanine (G)1764A mutation in the C1 clone was investigated by site-directed mutagenesis. As a result, the genotype C1 clone exhibited significantly higher replication capacity than the B2 clone. Counterintuitively, reverting the A1762T/G1764A mutation in the C1 clone to wild-type further enhanced its replication, indicating this mutation was not the primary driver of its high replicative fitness. In conclusion, HBV genotype C1 possesses a greater inherent replication capacity than B2, independent of the classic basal core promoter (BCP) mutation, providing a virological explanation for its association with severe disease outcomes in co-infection.

title: Autophagy-related gene expression is associated with fibrosis severity in chronic hepatitis B and fatty liver disease
abstract: Autophagy regulates hepatocyte survival, stellate cell activation and inflammation, but its transcriptional correlates in human liver fibrosis are poorly defined. In liver biopsy transcriptomes from 124 patients with chronic hepatitis B, 20 autophagy-related genes differed nominally between fibrotic and non-fibrotic tissue. Co-expression network analysis prioritized CCL2 , MYC , CDKN1A and CAPN2 , whose expression correlated with immune cell signatures and was positively associated with fibrosis stage after adjustment for inflammation grade, age and sex. An exploratory 15-gene neural-network classifier had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.982; bootstrap validation of a re-implemented development procedure gave an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.865, and the classifier had an AUC of 0.833 (95% confidence interval, 0.556–1.000) in whole blood from six healthy individuals and six with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. In two independent cohorts with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, expression of CCL2 , CAPN2 and CDKN1A , but not MYC , was higher in advanced than in mild fibrosis (n = 72), and that of all four genes was higher in fibrotic than in non-fibrotic liver (n = 112), largely owing to cirrhotic samples. These genes warrant further study as markers of fibrosis severity; their cellular sources and roles in fibrosis are unknown.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 124 名 慢性乙型肝炎 患者的肝活检转录组,确定了 20 个自噬相关基因,这些基因在纤维化组织和非纤维化组织之间存在显着差异。它还检查了两名患有非酒精性脂肪肝的独立 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了共表达网络分析来对基因进行优先排序,并使用引导方法开发和验证了探索性 15 基因神经网络分类器。
elements_zh.main_results: 分类器的接收者操作特征曲线 (AUC) 下的表观面积为 0.982,但重新实施的开发程序的引导验证给出的乐观校正 AUC 为 0.865。在来自 6 名健康个体和 6 名乙型肝炎相关肝硬化患者的全血中,分类器的 AUC 为 0.833(95% 置信区间,0.556-1.000)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,CCL2、CAPN2 和 CDKN1A 可能作为纤维化严重程度的潜在标志物,尽管它们的细胞来源和在纤维化中的作用仍不清楚。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些基因可以为未来纤维化严重程度标记物的研究提供信息,可能有助于开发与乙型肝炎相关的肝脏疾病的诊断工具。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于使用探索性分类器以及健康个体和肝硬化患者的样本量较小而受到限制,导致置信度评估适中。
