title: Peripheral Blood Natural Killer Cell Quantity, Phenotype, and Function Across the Clinical Spectrum of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection: A Scoping Review
abstract: This scoping review aims to systematically map and critically examine the available evidence on the quantity, phenotype, and function of peripheral blood natural killer (NK) cells across the clinical spectrum of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including chronic HBV infection and hepatitis, HBV-related liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, and HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although NK cells contribute to antiviral immunity, immune regulation, and tumor surveillance, findings concerning their circulating frequency, phenotypic characteristics, and functional responses remain heterogeneous. Differences in clinical populations, disease classification, antiviral treatment, blood sample processing, flow cytometric gating strategies, measurement denominators, and functional assay conditions may limit direct comparisons between studies. The review will be guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), with additional attention to transparent reporting of literature searches using PRISMA-S. Eligible evidence will primarily comprise original human studies reporting at least one peripheral blood NK-cell outcome related to quantity, phenotype, or function in populations with chronic HBV infection or HBV-associated liver disease. Studies involving mixed HCC etiologies will be considered for HBV-specific synthesis only where relevant subgroup findings can be identified separately. Peripheral blood findings will be distinguished from intrahepatic and tumor-infiltrating NK-cell measurements. The review will map NK-cell frequencies and absolute counts, CD56bright and CD56dim subsets, activating and inhibitory receptor profiles, and functional measurements such as cytokine production, degranulation, cytotoxicity, and antibody-dependent responses. Particular attention will be given to whether quantitative and functional outcomes were assessed in comparable populations, at the same time points, and under sufficiently similar experimental conditions. Preliminary literature searching, bibliographic data collection, deduplication, and targeted examination of selected publications have already been undertaken before registration. The registration will document the current stage of the review and specify the procedures for subsequent study selection, data charting, evidence synthesis, and protocol amendments. Earlier activities will not be represented as prospectively preregistered. Artificial intelligence tools have assisted with preliminary bibliographic organization, methodological planning, and exploration of the literature. Their use will be documented transparently. Decisions concerning study eligibility, extracted evidence, interpretation, and final conclusions will remain subject to human review and verification against original sources. The anticipated outcome is an evidence map identifying the distribution of research across HBV-related clinical conditions, the extent to which NK-cell quantity, phenotype, and function have been examined, major sources of methodological heterogeneity, and areas where evidence is limited or insufficiently comparable. The findings are intended to inform future clinical immunology and hepatology research and the design of more standardized investigations of peripheral blood NK cells in HBV-associated liver disease.

title: Interpretability-driven feature engineering enables compact and accurate multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) often trades predictive performance against interpretability. This study develops an interpretability-driven feature engineering framework for multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B. A total of 36,024 hospitalization records from 22,001 patients were included. The framework integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based main and interaction effects was used to construct compact machine learning models for classifying disease non-progression, liver cirrhosis (LC), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). SHAP main effects selected the top 15 features per outcome; TreeSHAP interactions selected four pairwise terms. Performance was evaluated using patient-level data splitting, temporal validation, and independent external validation, with calibration and decision-curve analyses. The full-feature models achieved superior discrimination (AUCs: 0.927, 0.897, and 0.899) for classifying hospitalization-recorded disease non-progression, LC, and HCC, respectively. The corresponding compact models maintained strong discrimination (AUCs: 0.911, 0.882, and 0.890) with 80.8% fewer features. Interaction models yielded subtle AUC shifts (AUCs: 0.912, 0.881, and 0.891) while characterizing potential clinical joint-effect patterns. Temporal validation yielded AUCs of 0.863, 0.827, and 0.847, while external validation yielded AUCs of 0.829, 0.865, and 0.827, respectively. The framework produced compact and transparent models for contemporaneous risk stratification in clinical practice, seamlessly uniting predictive accuracy with multi-level interpretability.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 共纳入 22,001 名患者的 36,024 条住院记录。集成基于 SHapley 加法解释 (SHAP) 的主效应和交互效应的框架用于构建紧凑的机器学习模型,用于对疾病无进展、肝硬化 (LC) 和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 进行分类。

title_zh: 可解释性驱动的特征工程可实现 慢性乙型肝炎 住院时紧凑且准确的多结果风险分层
source_body_en: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) often trades predictive performance against interpretability. This study develops an interpretability-driven feature engineering framework for multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B. A total of 36,024 hospitalization records from 22,001 patients were included. The framework integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based main and interaction effects was used to construct compact machine learning models for classifying disease non-progression, liver cirrhosis (LC), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). SHAP main effects selected the top 15 features per outcome; TreeSHAP interactions selected four pairwise terms. Performance was evaluated using patient-level data splitting, temporal validation, and independent external validation, with calibration and decision-curve analyses. The full-feature models achieved superior discrimination (AUCs: 0.927, 0.897, and 0.899) for classifying hospitalization-recorded disease non-progression, LC, and HCC, respectively. The corresponding compact models maintained strong discrimination (AUCs: 0.911, 0.882, and 0.890) with 80.8% fewer features. Interaction models yielded subtle AUC shifts (AUCs: 0.912, 0.881, and 0.891) while characterizing potential clinical joint-effect patterns. Temporal validation yielded AUCs of 0.863, 0.827, and 0.847, while external validation yielded AUCs of 0.829, 0.865, and 0.827, respectively. The framework produced compact and transparent models for contemporaneous risk stratification in clinical practice, seamlessly uniting predictive accuracy with multi-level interpretability.
abstract_zh: 临床人工智能 (AI) 通常会以预测性能与可解释性为代价。本研究开发了一种可解释性驱动的特征工程框架,用于 慢性乙型肝炎 住院时的多结果风险分层。共纳入 22,001 名患者的 36,024 条住院记录。集成基于 SHapley 加法解释 (SHAP) 的主效应和交互效应的框架用于构建紧凑的机器学习模型,用于对疾病无进展、肝硬化 (LC) 和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 进行分类。SHAP 主效应选择每个结果的前 15 个特征;TreeSHAP 交互选择了四个成对项。使用患者级数据分割、时间验证和独立外部验证以及校准和决策曲线分析来评估性能。全特征模型在对住院记录的疾病无进展、LC 和 HCC 进行分类方面分别实现了卓越的区分度(AUC:0.927、0.897 和 0.899)。相应的紧凑模型保持了很强的辨别力(AUC:0.911、0.882 和 0.890),特征减少了 80.8%。相互作用模型产生了微妙的 AUC 变化(AUC:0.912、0.881 和 0.891),同时表征了潜在的临床联合效应模式。时间验证产生的 AUC 分别为 0.863、0.827 和 0.847,而外部验证产生的 AUC 分别为 0.829、0.865 和 0.827。该框架为临床实践中的同期风险分层生成了紧凑而透明的模型,将预测准确性与多级可解释性无缝结合起来。

title: GAMBARAN HASIL PEMERIKSAAN ANTIBODI HEPATITIS B DAN HEPATITIS C PADA IBU HAMIL DENGAN METODE IMUNOKROMATOGRAFI DI PUSKESMAS SIDOARJO
abstract: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C are infectious diseases that can be transmitted from pregnant women to their babies during pregnancy, childbirth, or after birth. Screening examinations in pregnant women are important as an early detection effort to prevent vertical transmission. This study aimed to determine the profile of Hepatitis B antibody (HBsAb) and Hepatitis C antibody (Anti-HCV) test results among pregnant women using the immunochromatographic method at the Sidoarjo Community Health Center. This study employed a descriptive research design. The research was conducted at the Laboratory of the Sidoarjo Community Health Center from January to February 2026, involving 40 pregnant women who attended antenatal care (ANC) examinations. Testing was performed using the rapid immunochromatographic method on blood samples collected from the respondents to detect HBsAb and Anti-HCV antibodies. The results showed that, based on age, most respondents were in the 20–35 years age group, accounting for 32 individuals (80%). Based on gestational age, the majority of respondents were in the first trimester, totaling 22 individuals (55%). The HBsAb examination results indicated that 38 respondents (95%) were non-reactive and 2 respondents (5%) were reactive. Meanwhile, the Anti-HCV examination results showed that all 40 respondents (100%) were non-reactive. It is important for pregnant women to undergo Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C screening as a preventive measure to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission. ABSTRAK Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C merupakan penyakit infeksi yang beresiko menular dari ibu hamil kepada bayi selama kehamilan, persalinan, maupun setelah kelahiran. Pemeriksaan skrining pada ibu hamil penting dilakukan sebagai upaya deteksi dini untuk mencegah terjadinya penularan vertikal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui gambaran hasil pemeriksaan antibodi Hepatitis B (HBsAb) dan antibodi Hepatitis C (Anti-HCV) pada ibu hamil menggunakan metode imunokromatografi di Puskesmas Sidoarjo. Jenis penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif. Penelitian dilakukan di Laboratorium Puskesmas Sidoarjo pada bulan Januari–Februari 2026 dengan jumlah responden sebanyak 40 ibu hamil yang melakukan pemeriksaan antenatal care (ANC). Pemeriksaan dilakukan menggunakan metode imunokromatografi rapid test terhadap sampel darah responden untuk mendeteksi HBsAb dan Anti-HCV. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa berdasarkan usia, sebagian besar responden berada pada kelompok usia 20–35 tahun sebanyak 32 orang (80%). Berdasarkan usia kehamilan, mayoritas responden berada pada trimester I sebanyak 22 orang (55%). Hasil pemeriksaan HBsAb menunjukkan sebanyak 38 responden (95%) non reaktif dan 2 responden (5%) reaktif. Sementara itu, hasil pemeriksaan Anti-HCV menunjukkan seluruh responden 40 orang (100%) non reaktif. Penting bagi ibu hamil untuk melakukan pemeriksaan Hepatitis B maupun Hepatitis C sebagai upaya pencegahan risiko penularan ibu hamil kepada bayi.

title: Interferon therapy reduces incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with high risk of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND The proportion of patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is as high as 85.69% among HCC patients in China. Current anti-HBV drugs include nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) and interferon (IFN). AIM To compare the impact of NAs and IFN therapy on the occurrence of HCC in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC. METHODS We enrolled 368 patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC, and 120 received subcutaneous injections of IFN, with or without NAs, constituting the IFN group. The remaining 248 patients were assigned to the NAs group, and received treatment with NAs alone. title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Metabolically, the co-infected group had a significantly higher ornithine-to-arginine ratio. Mediation analysis suggested that PMN-MDSCs accounted for approximately 45% of the total effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. sinensis co-infection was associated with immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and elevated ornithine-to-arginine ratio, resulting in suppressed IFN-γ production despite normal liver enzyme levels.

title: DISTRIBUTION OF FIVE HEPATITIS B VIRUS MARKERS IN HIV INFECTED AND UNINFECTED INJECTING DRUG USERS IN COASTAL KENYA
abstract: Aims: This study determined HBV sero-markers profile in HIV-1 infected (n=157) and uninfected (n=214) IDUs from Mombasa, Kenya HIV-1 diagnosis was performed using DetermineTM and UnigoldTM rapid tests. Methodology: The CD4+ T cells were enumerated using the FacsCalibur flow cytometer and categorized according to the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) immunological staging criteria. HBV seroprofile was determined using HBV-5 panel rapid test cassettes. Clinical staging was based on serological profile of the five HBV markers. Results: HBsAg (P=0.004) and HBcAb-IgM (P=0.008) positivities were higher in the HIV-1 infected compared to the uninfected individuals while the opposite was observed for HBsAb positivity (P=0.019). Rates of acute (P=0.033) and chronic (P=0.021) clinical stages were higher in the HIV-1 infected compared to the uninfected individuals but the inverse was noticed for vaccine type response rate (P=0.008). Only genotype A, sub-genotype A1 was detected with higher frequencies noted in the HIV-1 infected (n=12) compared to the uninfected (n=4) individuals. Conclusion: HBsAg and HBcAb-IgM sero-markers and acute and chronic clinical categories are higher while HBsAb sero-marker and vaccine type response stage are lower in HIV-1 infected compared to uninfected IDUs at Mombasa, Kenya. Taken together, HIV infected injection drug users are at risk of acquiring HBV and progressing to chronic infection.
journal: Global Journal of Research in Medicine and Dentistry

title: Hospital-linked and community-based viral hepatitis screening among Romanian migrants in Seville: A feasibility study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Romanian migrants may be at increased risk of viral hepatitis because many originate from countries with intermediate or high endemicity. Targeted, culturally adapted screening strategies are therefore needed to improve case finding and prevention. Our aim was to explore the feasibility of two sequential viral hepatitis screening strategies among Romanian migrants living in Seville, Spain. METHODS: We conducted a two-phase opportunistic screening study. Phase 1 was a Consulate-facilitated, hospital-based program using venipuncture and comprehensive serological testing. Phase 2 was a community-based program delivered at an Orthodox church using rapid diagnostic tests. Demographic characteristics, recruitment output, serological findings, fibrosis markers, and linkage to care were recorded. RESULTS: Of the total participants (n=54), the number of individuals screened was higher in the community-based intervention (n=39) than the hospital-based program (n=15). Median age was 48.5 (39.5-58) years, and 74.1% were women. No active viral hepatitis infections were identified. In phase 1, 66.7% of participants (10/15) lacked hepatitis B immunity and were candidates for vaccination, while 6.7% (1/15) had non-invasive markers compatible with intermediate fibrosis and required further assessment. In phase 2, 2.6% of participants (1/39) had antibodies against hepatitis C virus with documented prior cured infection. CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot study, community-based screening in a familiar religious setting appeared more productive and operationally feasible for short-term recruitment than a hospital-based approach. These findings support the feasibility of decentralized strategies to improve engagement and may inform future micro-elimination programs in migrant populations.

source_records.title: Hospital-linked and community-based viral hepatitis screening among Romanian migrants in Seville: A feasibility study.
source_records.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Romanian migrants may be at increased risk of viral hepatitis because many originate from countries with intermediate or high endemicity. Targeted, culturally adapted screening strategies are therefore needed to improve case finding and prevention. Our aim was to explore the feasibility of two sequential viral hepatitis screening strategies among Romanian migrants living in Seville, Spain. METHODS: We conducted a two-phase opportunistic screening study. Phase 1 was a Consulate-facilitated, hospital-based program using venipuncture and comprehensive serological testing. Phase 2 was a community-based program delivered at an Orthodox church using rapid diagnostic tests. Demographic characteristics, recruitment output, serological findings, fibrosis markers, and linkage to care were recorded. RESULTS: Of the total participants (n=54), the number of individuals screened was higher in the community-based intervention (n=39) than the hospital-based program (n=15). Median age was 48.5 (39.5-58) years, and 74.1% were women. No active viral hepatitis infections were identified. In phase 1, 66.7% of participants (10/15) lacked hepatitis B immunity and were candidates for vaccination, while 6.7% (1/15) had non-invasive markers compatible with intermediate fibrosis and required further assessment. In phase 2, 2.6% of participants (1/39) had antibodies against hepatitis C virus with documented prior cured infection. CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot study, community-based screening in a familiar religious setting appeared more productive and operationally feasible for short-term recruitment than a hospital-based approach. These findings support the feasibility of decentralized strategies to improve engagement and may inform future micro-elimination programs in migrant populations.

title: Prevalence of Hepatitis B surface antigen positivity among pregnant women in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: This project hosts the protocol and related materials for a systematic review and meta-analysis estimating the pooled prevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity among pregnant women in the 22 countries of the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region. Observational studies reporting HBsAg seroprevalence in pregnant women will be identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and regional databases. Study quality will be assessed with the JBI checklist for prevalence studies, and pooled prevalence will be estimated using a random-effects model, with subgroup analyses by country, study period and setting.

title: Prevalence of Reactive Screening Markers for HIV, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and Syphilis Among Blood Donors at the Provincial Hospital of Sarh, Chad: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: Blood transfusion safety remains a challenge in resource-limited settings. This study estimated the prevalence of reactive screening markers for HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and syphilis among blood donors at Sarh Provincial Hospital, Chad. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study used blood bank register data from 18 September to 18 November 2023. Of 2,868 records identified, 27 were excluded and 2,841 donors were analyzed. Screening used rapid diagnostic tests; confirmatory testing was unavailable. Prevalence estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Results: Participants included 2,173 men (76.49%) and 668 women (23.51%); 97.75% were family/replacement donors. Reactive markers were HBV 275/2,841 (9.68%; 95% CI 8.64– 10.83), syphilis 177/2,841 (6.23%; 95% CI 5.39– 7.18), HCV 104/2,841 (3.66%; 95% CI 3.03– 4.42), and HIV 95/2,841 (3.34%; 95% CI 2.74– 4.07). Overall, 584 donors (20.56%) had at least one reactive marker, and 64 (2.25%) had multiple-marker reactivity. No significant sex differences were observed; age trends were not significant for HBV or HCV. Conclusion: HBV and syphilis were the most frequent reactive screening markers. Because confirmatory testing was not available, results represent screening-marker reactivity rather than laboratory-confirmed infection. Findings are limited to this hospital and the two-month study period. Strengthening voluntary non-remunerated donation, quality assurance, confirmatory testing, and surveillance may improve blood safety. Keywords: reactive screening marker, HIV, HBV, HCV, syphilis, blood donors, Sarh Provincial Hospital, Chad

title: ENFERMEDADES INFECTOCONTAGIOSAS ASOCIADAS A HEMODIÁLISIS: PREVALENCIA DE INFECCIÓN POR HEPATITIS B EN PACIENTES RENALES
abstract: La infección por el virus de la hepatitis B (VHB) es un problema infectocontagioso muy relevante en pacientes con enfermedad renal crónica que se encuentran recibiendo hemodiálisis. La vulnerabilidad es debido a múltiples exposiciones a sangre por medio del acceso vascular y la manipulación del circuito extracorpóreo, junto con la necesidad de atención médica constante. Se realizó una revisión bibliográfica narrativa mediante búsquedas sistemáticas en bases de datos biomédicas, priorizando estudios recientes, metaanálisis y guías clínicas sobre el VHB, hemodiálisis, bioseguridad, vacunación y diagnóstico molecular. Los datos analizados demuestran que el VHB sigue siendo un desafío clínico significativo, aunque su prevalencia varía según la región y el marcador diagnóstico empleado, se considera que esta población es especialmente susceptible debido a la disfunción inmunitaria asociada a la uremia, la exposición repetida a procedimientos invasivos y posibles fallas en las medidas de control de infecciones. Asimismo, la infección oculta por VHB provoca que la carga real de la enfermedad se subestime cuando el tamizaje se basa únicamente en el antígeno de superficie (HBsAg). Adicionalmente, la respuesta inmunológica a la vacunación es menor en estos pacientes, lo que exige esquemas de refuerzo, monitorizar periódicamente los títulos anti-HBs y considerar la revacunación en pacientes de alto riesgo. La prevención de la hepatitis B (VHB) en la hemodiálisis debe ser un proceso recurrente y no un proceso aislado. La vacunación oportuna, el cribado inicial, los controles periódicos de salud, el uso de pruebas moleculares y el cumplimiento estricto de la bioseguridad constituyen los principales pilares para reducir el riesgo de transmisión. En este sentido, una alta frecuencia de VHB en las unidades de diálisis refleja indirectamente la calidad de las medidas preventivas y el cumplimiento de las prácticas de protección.

title: Serological and molecular epidemiology of hepatitis D virus: a four-year single-center retrospective analysis
abstract: Aim To assess the serological and molecular epidemiology of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) infections by analyzing HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), Anti-HDV, and HDV ribonucleic acid (RNA) test results from May 2021 to May 2025 at Ordu University Training and Research Hospital. Methods This single-center retrospective study used Laboratory Information Management System records. Patients aged 0-100 years with at least one request for an HBsAg, Anti-HDV, or HDV RNA test were included. To minimize duplication, only the earliest record per patient for each marker was analyzed. Positivity rates were summarized descriptively and compared by sex and age using Pearson’s chi-square test. Results Among 316,375 individuals tested for HBsAg, 8,054 (2.5%) were positive. HBsAg positivity was higher in men than in women ( P = .0011). Positivity was low among those P > .05). HDV RNA was requested in 64 patients, and 3 (4.68%) were positive. Conclusion HBsAg positivity suggests an intermediate level of HBV endemicity in our region, whereas Anti-HDV seropositivity appears low. Because Anti-HDV and HDV RNA testing were not systematically performed in all HBsAg-positive individuals, the true burden of HDV infection may be underestimated. Standardized screening strategies among HBsAg-positive patients are warranted to better define regional HDV epidemiology.

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram to Predict Recompensation in Patients With HBV-Related Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: Limited studies have investigated the predictors of hepatic recompensation in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). Establishing a clinically applicable predictive model for recompensation in ACLF patients is of critical importance. A total of 304 HBV-ACLF patients were included in the study, 169 patients as training cohort and 135 patients as validation cohort. In the training cohort, 72 patients (42.6%) achieved recompensation within the first year following an ACLF episode, whereas 87 patients (64.4%) in the validation cohort achieved recompensation during the same period. Age, alpha-fetoprotein, total bilirubin, white blood cell count, hepatic encephalopathy, and gastrointestinal bleeding were selected for inclusion in the model. The nomogram demonstrated excellent discriminative ability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.842 (95% CI: 0.784-0.900) in the training cohort and 0.855 (95% CI: 0.785-0.926) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed strong agreement between predicted and observed recompensation rates. DCA further confirmed the model's clinical utility for decision-making. This model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to the MELD score, MELD-Na score, and MELD 3.0 score. The developed nomogram provides an accurate and clinically applicable tool for predicting recompensation likelihood, enhancing personalized management of HBV-ACLF patients.

title: Beyond HIV prevention: Reframing PrEP clinics as hubs for viral hepatitis prevention and elimination.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The expansion of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has created a growing network of prevention services that regularly engage people who may also be exposed or susceptible to viral hepatitis. PrEP care is inherently longitudinal, involving repeated clinical assessment, laboratory testing, counselling and vaccination review. These features make PrEP clinics uniquely positioned to contribute to viral hepatitis prevention and elimination. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence on the integration of viral hepatitis prevention, screening, diagnosis and care within PrEP services, and propose a practical framework, the PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade, for translating the principle of integrated HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infection services into routine clinical practice. METHODS: A focused literature search was conducted between 1 May and 8 August 2026 across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the WHO Global Index Medicus, using documented search strings supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. We prioritized studies conducted among PrEP users or within PrEP programmes, together with relevant international guidelines and policy documents. Records were screened in two stages against predefined eligibility criteria, and the findings were mapped to the steps of the cascade. Evidence was sought on HAV and HBV vaccination coverage, HBV seroprevalence and susceptibility, the relationship between tenofovir-based PrEP and HBV prevention, HCV epidemiology among PrEP users, simplified diagnostic strategies and integrated service delivery models. Given the heterogeneity of study designs and outcomes, the literature was synthesized narratively rather than through formal meta-analysis. Interventions and indicators for each cascade step were then summarized in an evidence-linked implementation and monitoring table. RESULTS: The evidence consistently demonstrates that vaccination gaps for HAV and HBV persist among PrEP users, with suboptimal initiation and completion rates across settings; that HBV susceptibility remains common among individuals entering PrEP care; and that tenofovir-based PrEP, while offering incidental HBV protection, should not substitute for vaccination. HCV epidemiology among PrEP users is heterogeneous, supporting risk-adapted testing strategies, while simplified diagnostic pathways and self-testing approaches have shown promise for HCV. The PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade proposed here offers a structured, implementable framework connecting vaccination, case finding, linkage to care and longitudinal reassessment within the existing PrEP pathway. The cascade is presented as a detailed figure and as an implementation and monitoring table linking each step to supporting evidence, candidate interventions and measurable indicators, without assigning responsibilities to specific providers. Implementation challenges include variability in PrEP delivery models, the need for equity-oriented approaches and the implications of long-acting and tenofovir-sparing PrEP regimens for HBV prevention. CONCLUSION: PrEP programmes have created a longitudinal prevention infrastructure that extends beyond HIV prevention. HAV vaccination, HBV screening and vaccination, identification of chronic HBV infection, HCV testing, simplified diagnostics, treatment linkage and surveillance for reinfection can all be incorporated at different points of the PrEP pathway. The next step is to move from opportunistic to intentional integration. PrEP clinics should be reframed as integrated viral hepatitis prevention and elimination hubs, translating global strategies into routine care and contributing to viral hepatitis elimination goals. The question is no longer whether PrEP clinics can contribute to viral hepatitis elimination, but whether the global health community will deliberately invest in making this integration a reality.

title: Quantifying a Neglected Burden: Pregnancy-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Maternal Death in South Africa.
abstract: PURPOSE: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during pregnancy is rare, with the literature confined to isolated case reports and small series. Women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) face disproportionate risk due to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection acquired perinatally, HCC in noncirrhotic livers at a young age, and fertility rates nearly three times those of Europe. To our knowledge, we report the largest cohort of pregnancy-associated HCC from SSA, drawn from a single South African center, and the first quantitative estimate of regional disparity versus Europe. METHODS: Pregnant women with HCC at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, over 24 years (2001-2025) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry. A model integrating HCC incidence, age-at-diagnosis, fertility rates, and 1-year mortality compared the probability of pregnancy-associated HCC and maternal death in SSA versus Europe. RESULTS: Of the 728 registry patients, 192 (26.4%) were female and 10 (5.2%) were pregnant or within 1 year postpartum. The median age was 32.5 (IQR, 28.5-35.3), 70% had chronic HBV infection, and three had cirrhosis. Seven (70%) died, six within 90 days. Two patients survived beyond 10 years following curative resection. Four pregnancies ended in intrauterine fetal demise and five in live births. The modeled probability of pregnancy-associated HCC was 16 per 100,000 women in SSA versus 0.14 per 100,000 in Europe-a 114-fold difference-with a 187-fold greater risk of maternal death. CONCLUSION: Pregnancy-associated HCC in SSA is a quantifiable, preventable contributor to maternal mortality-nearly two orders of magnitude greater than in Europe. HBV endemicity, early-onset noncirrhotic HCC, and high fertility rates create a hostile environment for women of reproductive age. HBV-aware liver surveillance in antenatal care, strengthened prevention of mother-to-child transmission programs, and improved maternal mortality data systems are urgently needed.

title: Clinical Significance of Indeterminate Antibody to Hepatitis C in Cancer Patients
abstract: Most patients with cancer are screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection using an antibody to HCV (anti-HCV) test. However, the importance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result is unknown. We investigated the clinical significance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result in cancer patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of cancer patients screened for HCV infection using ARCHITECT Anti-HCV at our institution between October 2016 and July 2024. Patients were categorized based on their anti-HCV results as patients with indeterminate anti-HCV and undetectable HCV-RNA in the absence of HCV treatment, and patients with reactive anti-HCV and chronic infection. We compared the two groups using univariable analyses and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Of the 112,180 patients screened with anti-HCV, 114 (0.1%) had indeterminate results; 101 of them with confirmed cancer were further analysed. Anti-HCV testing was repeated in 24 (24%) patients; most (84%) had non-reactive (46%) or indeterminate (38%) results. Among the 101 patients with indeterminate anti-HCV, 98 (97%) did not have proven HCV infection, but 3 (3%) had HCV infection. Multivariable analysis showed that male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.40-3.53, p < 0.001), age ≥ 60 years (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.01-2.56, p = 0.046), hepatitis B or HIV coinfection (aOR 3.13, 95% CI 1.21-8.11, p = 0.019) and cirrhosis (aOR 6.67, 95% CI 2.05-21.69, p = 0.002) were more likely to have chronic than an indeterminate anti-HCV result. Indeterminate anti-HCV results are uncommon in cancer patients and rarely indicate HCV infection.

source_records.abstract: Most patients with cancer are screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection using an antibody to HCV (anti-HCV) test. However, the importance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result is unknown. We investigated the clinical significance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result in cancer patients. Patients were categorized based on their anti-HCV results as patients with indeterminate anti-HCV and undetectable HCV-RNA in the absence of HCV treatment, and patients with reactive anti-HCV and chronic infection. We compared the two groups using univariable analyses and multivariable logistic regression analysis. title: SUMOylated DDX3 Promotes HBV Replication and Tumor Growth of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TRIM28‐DDX3‐KLF4α Signaling Axis
abstract: ABSTRACT DDX3 has dual biological functions of regulating cell proliferation and antiviral effects. Herein, we focus on SUMOylation‐mediated DDX3 in the interplay from hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to HBV‐associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV‐HCC) progression. We identified dynamic regulation of SUMOylation and DeSUMOylation of DDX3 at four key lysine (K) residues (K81/K208/K215/K564) in response to HBV infection. During the early stage of HBV acute infection, SENP1 interacts with DDX3 to keep DDX3 deSUMOylation for inhibiting HBV replication. During persistent HBV replication, as SENP1 downregulation and HBV polymerase accumulation, DDX3 disassociates with SENP1 to bind with TRIM28, which induces DDX3 SUMOylation. Meanwhile, SUMOylated DDX3 enhances alternative splicing of KLF4 mRNAs to generate KLF4α isoform that involves in Cyclin D1‐mediated cell cycle progression, weakens tumor suppressor function of DDX3 and promotes HBV‐HCC. Moreover, DDX3 expression is positively correlated with KLF4 mRNA, and high DDX3 level with low TRIM28 expression indicates a better overall survival for HBV‐HCC patients. Our findings reveal the dynamic regulation between SUMOylation and deSUMOylation of DDX3, including mediating HBV gene transcription, virus antigen secretion, and cell proliferation. Furthermore, the TRIM28‐DDX3‐KLF4 axis as a novel therapeutic target for HBV‐HCC, exhibiting the dual ability to inhibit tumor progression and disrupt the HBV–host interaction.

title: Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom and its bioactive peptides tertiapin and apamin modulate the proteome of SARS-CoV-2-infected cells.
abstract: The continuing emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variants highlights the need for host-directed antiviral strategies with specific molecular mechanisms. Honeybee (Apis mellifera) venom (HBV) contains bioactive peptides with immunomodulatory and membrane-active properties, yet their effects on SARS-CoV-2 infection remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated the antiviral activity and proteomic impact of whole HBV and two venom-derived peptides, apamin (APA) and tertiapin (TERT), in human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2-expressing HEK293 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 spike-pseudotyped lentiviral particles. Cell viability and membrane integrity assays showed that HBV, APA, and TERT exerted limited cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations. In pseudovirus infectivity assays, HBV displayed the strongest inhibitory effect, reducing viral infectivity to 61.3% at 2 μg/mL, whereas APA reduced it to 73.3% at 0.5 μg/mL, and TERT showed weaker inhibitory activity. Comparative nano-liquid chromatography matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization tandem mass spectrometry revealed treatment-associated remodelling of the host-cell proteome. A shared signature of 215 proteins across HBV-, APA-, and TERT-treated infected cells was enriched in binding and catalytic activity, translational proteins, metabolite interconversion enzymes, cytoskeletal proteins, and pathways linked to integrin, Wnt, interferon, and Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription signalling. Protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted functional clusters associated with cytoplasmic translation, viral mRNA translation, and the Sec61 translocon complex, with EFTUD2, EPRS1, and HSPA4 emerging as central hubs. HBV treatment additionally promoted immune-related and interferon-stimulated gene products, including factors involved in innate antiviral defence, cytoskeletal organization, ion transport, and membrane structural reinforcement. These findings suggest that HBV reduces SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus infectivity through a multifactorial host-directed mechanism involving antiviral signalling, cellular architecture, and proteostasis, supporting further investigation of bee venom-derived compounds as antiviral agents.

title: Management Challenge in a Known case of Chronic Kidney Disease on Immuno-Suppressive Agents Now Presenting with Acute Viral Hepatitis
abstract: Background: Tubulo-Interstitial Nephritis (TIN) is a nonsuppurative inflammatory disease of the kidney interstitium and if chronic, almost always progresses to Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). Hemodialysis is frequently performed as renal replacement therapy. However, to treat the underlying cause of CKD, like in autoimmune cases immunosuppressive agents are needed in addition. Patients undergoing hemodialysis are at higher risk of developing blood borne infections such as HBV and HCV. Due to impaired immunity in CKD, TIN patients on immunosuppressive therapy becoming HBV infected, warrants a clear treatment limitation like withholding of immunosuppressants as the viral replication soars high, increasing the chances of developing chronicity and viral mutants. Anti-viral drugs are very helpful for HBV infection control in these patients. The purpose of this case report is to draw the clinicians' attention towards early diagnosis and management of HBV infection among such groups of CKD patients, as it can cause higher morbidity and mortality, if not appropriately addressed. Case Presentation: We report here a female of 37 years age suffering from CKD due to TIN, priorly on Maintenance Hemodialysis (MHD) for 3 months followed by immune-suppressive agents for next 3 months with evident clinical improvement. She suddenly developed silent deep jaundice and health deterioration with hepatitis B positivity and high viral load on testing. Antiviral administration and withdrawal of immunosuppressive therapy showed significant improvement over a short span of time. She was never vaccinated against Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) prior to or during her treatment. Conclusion: CKD patients on renal replacement with dialysis, immunosuppressants and steroid, acquiring HBV infection is a major concern. The aim here is to highlight few points for management aspects of HBV infection in such group of patients, which are not commonly, but should necessarily, be a part of the protocoled medical practice in our country. Moreover, prevention of infection by vaccination and infection control measure should be strictly followed. Chatt Maa Shi Hosp Med Coll J; Vol.25 (2); July 2026; Page 125-128

title: Antiangiogenic class and trial population are confounded in first-line immunotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma: a Bayesian network meta-analysis of nine randomised trials
abstract: Abstract Background First-line therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) combines an immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) with one of two antiangiogenic backbones: an anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody or a VEGFR-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). No head-to-head trial exists, and successive network meta-analyses have ranked the two classes and reported class-level probabilities as estimates of a drug-class property. Objective To estimate the class comparison and, separately, to test whether a class effect is identifiable from the aggregate trial data on which such rankings are based. Methods Nine randomised trials (5,333 patients) were synthesised in a Bayesian random-effects network anchored on sorafenib. Because each treatment appears in a single trial, between-study heterogeneity is not identifiable from the data; it was therefore specified using the external empirical predictive distributions of Turner et al., and every efficacy estimate reported here is conditional on that externally sourced prior. Outcomes were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response (ORR) and grade ≥3 adverse events. Five effect modifiers were pre-specified; their joint distribution across trials was examined before interpreting any class-level estimate. Results Three regimens improved OS over sorafenib: sintilimab plus bevacizumab (HR 0.57, 95% credible interval 0.35–0.92), finotonlimab plus bevacizumab (0.60, 0.37–0.99) and camrelizumab plus rivoceranib (0.64, 0.41–0.99). The posterior probability favouring the anti-VEGF-antibody class was 75.0% for OS, 74.8% for ORR and 45.3% for PFS. These estimates are not interpretable as class effects. Treatment class, hepatitis B virus prevalence, macrovascular invasion and China-only enrolment were mutually collinear across trials (pairwise r = 0.81–0.91; HBV–China r = 0.87), so a survival advantage attributed to drug class is equally consistent with one attributable to the populations in which each class was tested. With nine trials, trial-level meta-regression is underpowered to separate the independent contributions of viral aetiology and geographic enrolment and is reported as hypothesis-generating only; no reweighting or prior specification separates them either, and sensitivity analyses moved the class probability only between 73.9% and 85.5% without altering this. The contrasts that do survive are those estimated within randomised comparisons: grade ≥3 hand-foot syndrome occurred with every TKI regimen (2–12%) and with none of the four anti-VEGF-antibody regimens, against 6.9–12% in the sorafenib arms of those same trials. Conclusions Class rankings in first-line HCC describe the evidence base rather than a property of the drugs. The collinearity of treatment class with viral aetiology and geographic region makes class attribution unidentifiable from aggregate data, irrespective of model choice, and this limitation applies to the published rankings as much as to ours. On GRADE-NMA the class-level indirect comparison was rated very low certainty, downgraded for unresolvable confounding by trial population. Separating drug class from trial population will require individual-patient-data analysis or head-to-head randomisation; until then, within-trial contrasts remain the defensible basis for class-level claims.

title: Targeting the Functional Cure: The Journey of HBV from Transmission to Therapeutic Vaccines
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) infection affects 262 million people worldwide, leading to over 820,000 deaths annually. The reason HBV has been a persistent issue for decades is that it is a non-cytopathic, liver-specific virus with the ability for persistent infection, which cannot be completely eliminated by drugs, eventually progressing to cirrhosis and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC). Although HBV seems to induce little innate immue activation, adaptive immune responses can mediate viral clearance and liver disease. This review aims to provide an overview of HBV epidemiology, transmission, immunopathogenesis, current treatment strategies and recent advances in therapeutic vaccine development. It further explores the challenges and future directions toward achieving a functional cure and strengthening global HBV control. Methodology: This review to published studies and articles by using PubMed and Google. Search strategy using appropriate keywords and title. Conclusion: Therapeutic vaccines are a very promissing immunotherapy strategy in the treatment of hepatitis B. IAHS Medical Journal Vol 9(1), June 2026;114-117

source_records.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) infection affects 262 million people worldwide, leading to over 820,000 deaths annually. The reason HBV has been a persistent issue for decades is that it is a non-cytopathic, liver-specific virus with the ability for persistent infection, which cannot be completely eliminated by drugs, eventually progressing to cirrhosis and Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC). Although HBV seems to induce little innate immue activation, adaptive immune responses can mediate viral clearance and liver disease. This review aims to provide an overview of HBV epidemiology, transmission, immunopathogenesis, current treatment strategies and recent advances in therapeutic vaccine development. It further explores the challenges and future directions toward achieving a functional cure and strengthening global HBV control. Methodology: This review to published studies and articles by using PubMed and Google. Search strategy using appropriate keywords and title. Conclusion: Therapeutic vaccines are a very promissing immunotherapy strategy in the treatment of hepatitis B. IAHS Medical Journal Vol 9(1), June 2026;114-117

title: Engineering the host microenvironment: the “double hit” of HBV subgenotype A1 and G1862T-driven oncogenesis
abstract: Introduction Hepatitis B virus (HBV) subgenotype A1 and its endemic G1862T mutation are associated with aggressive, early-onset hepatocellular carcinoma in South Africa. While classically studied via molecular pathways, the biomechanical modifications that prime the hepatic microenvironment for the Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) prior to oncogenesis remain largely unexplored. Methods Using a custom automated bioimaging pipeline and high-resolution confocal microscopy, macroscopic topology, extracellular matrix remodelling, and subcellular compartmentalisation in Huh-7 cells expressing wild-type and G1862T-mutant HBV were quantified. Junctional decoupling and active oncogenic translocation were mapped using ratiometric compartmental analyses. Results The viral backbone engineered a severe mechanical mismatch, inducing a massive bystander-associated upregulation of fibrogenic matrix proteins, F-actin depolymerisation, and significant E-cadherin internalisation. Topological analysis revealed severe, mutation-independent cellular compaction. Although both variants disrupted adherens junctions to a similar extent, the mutant induced an approximately 71% reduction in nuclear β-catenin levels relative to the WT and promoted its perinuclear accumulation, potentially facilitating highly efficient active nuclear translocation. Discussion A mechanobiological “Double Hit” paradigm is proposed. The wild-type HBV backbone (First Hit) acts as an active biomechanical engineer, destroying epithelial mechanoreciprocity to construct a dysplastic, EMT-associated pre-metastatic niche. This foundational structural wreckage creates the optimal, low-resistance environment necessary for the G1862T mutation (Second Hit). By capitalising on both the physical destabilisation and a host-driven proteotoxic stress response, the G1862T HBV efficiently hijacks the surviving β -catenin pool into the nucleus, in a more moderate way than the WT, providing a stealthy, proposed biophysical mechanism for the African enigma.

title: Noninvasive Diagnosis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Outside Guideline-Defined High-Risk Populations: Evolving Perspectives in the Era of MASLD.
abstract: Noninvasive imaging-based diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in high-risk patients currently relies on the radiological hallmark of arterial-phase hyperenhancement followed by delayed washout. These criteria were designed to achieve both a high positive predictive value and sufficient specificity when applied to well-defined target populations. However, the incidence of HCC is rising globally among individuals outside the traditional high-risk groups, including those with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly known as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease) and genetic predispositions. This shifting epidemiology poses challenges to the current noninvasive diagnostic strategies and the binary classification of patients as either "at high-risk" or "not at high-risk," which heavily depends on established risk factors such as chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and liver cirrhosis. Consequently, HCC in non-high-risk individuals is often diagnosed at more advanced stages, underscoring the urgent need for reliable and noninvasive diagnostic tools tailored to this demographic population. These challenges present opportunities for the radiology community to play a proactive role in addressing them. Given the heterogeneous risk factors among low- and intermediate-risk populations, integrated strategies incorporating imaging features, fibrosis stage, serum biomarkers, individualized risk models, and artificial intelligence-assisted cross-sectional imaging may help improve the noninvasive diagnosis of non-cirrhotic or metabolically driven HCC. This review summarizes the current performance and limitations of noninvasive diagnosis outside the conventional high-risk populations in the era of MASLD and highlights emerging diagnostic strategies that warrant further investigation as evidence continues to accumulate.

title: Annual change in estimated glomerular filtration rate and predictors of rapid kidney function decline among antiretroviral therapy-experienced older people with HIV in Uganda, sub-Saharan Africa: A cohort study
abstract: Abstract Introduction : Older people with HIV (PWH) receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) in sub-Saharan Africa are at high risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) while routine kidney function monitoring remains limited in this setting. We examined changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) per year and risk of rapid kidney function decline over 3 years among older PWH in Uganda. Methods Our cohort study included 500 PWH aged ≥ 60 years receiving ART at the Infectious Diseases Institute in Uganda who were followed between 2020–2024. We measured serum creatinine at each annual visit. We estimated predictors of annual eGFR change and rapid kidney function decline (defined as eGFR loss ≥5mL/min/1.73m 2 /year) in linear mixed effects and modified Poisson regression models, respectively. Results Among 500 PWH with a median age of 64 (interquartile range (IQR): 62,68) years, 49% were female, and their median eGFR was 75 (IQR: 60,92) mL/min/1.73m 2 at baseline. Over a median follow up of 2.95 years, the cohort experienced a -0.7 (IQR: -3.3,4.7) mL/min/1.73m 2 change in eGFR per year, and 76 (15.2%) participants developed rapid kidney function decline. Female sex (1.82 [95%CI:0.95–2.70]), use of integrase strand transfer inhibitors (2.50[95%CI:1.52–3.48]), higher CD4 cell count (0.21[95%CI:0.04–0.37]), and hepatitis B surface antigen positivity (4.19[95%CI:2.11–6.27]) at baseline were associated with improvement in eGFR (mL/min/1.73m 2 ) per year. Longer cumulative exposure to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) (relative risk (RR) = 1.33 (95%CI:1.11–1.60) per doubling of TDF exposure in years), and male sex (RR = 1.91 (95%CI:1.08–3.37)) were associated with a higher risk of rapid kidney function decline. A higher CD4 cell count (RR = 0.91 per 100 cells increase/ml; 95% CI: 0.84–0.99)) and use of integrase strand transfer inhibitors (RR = 0.41; 95%CI: 0.23–0.72) were associated with a reduced risk of rapid kidney function decline. Switching from TDF prior to or during the cohort did not mitigate the risk of rapid kidney function decline. Conclusions Among older PWH in sub-Saharan Africa, annual eGFR decline was mild overall and comparable to other aging populations. However, a subset of this population experienced rapid kidney function decline especially if they were males and those exposed to TDF, and these may need tailored or more frequent kidney function monitoring.

title: Prevalence and correlates of serological markers of HBV infectivity and recent infection among HBsAG-positive inmates in Ghanaian correctional facilities
abstract: Correctional facilities are recognized as high-risk settings for the transmission of blood-borne infections, including hepatitis B virus (HBV), owing to overcrowding, high-risk behaviours, and limited access to healthcare. Higher prevalence of HBV among incarcerated populations in Ghana compared with the general population highlights the need to evaluate serological markers associated with infectivity and recent infection. This study assessed the prevalence of hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) and immunoglobulin M antibodies to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc IgM) among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive inmates in correctional facilities in Ghana. A cross-sectional secondary analysis was conducted using 323 archived plasma samples from HBsAg-positive inmates collected during a nationwide prison survey. HBeAg and anti-HBc IgM were determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs). Associations between these serological markers and demographic, behavioural, clinical, and incarceration-related characteristics were evaluated. Of the 323 HBsAg-positive samples analysed, 91 (28.2%) were HBeAg positive and 16 (5.0%) were anti-HBc IgM positive. HBeAg positivity was significantly associated with prison type ( p < 0.001) and duration of incarceration ( p < 0.05). Most inmates who tested positive for anti-HBc IgM had been incarcerated for more than one year. However, no significant associations were observed between anti-HBc IgM positivity and the demographic variables examined. A substantial proportion of HBsAg-positive inmates had serological markers associated with increased HBV infectivity, while a small proportion had anti-HBc IgM, a marker that may indicate recent infection but can also occur during flares of chronic HBV infection. Although these findings highlight the potential for HBV transmission within correctional facilities, the cross-sectional design and absence of pre-incarceration serological data preclude confirmation of intra-prison transmission. Strengthened HBV screening, vaccination, clinical management, and longitudinal studies incorporating HBV DNA testing are warranted to better characterize HBV transmission in correctional settings.

title: Clinical Profile and Outcome of Acute Viral Hepatitis in Hospitalized Patients: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute viral hepatitis (AVH) is a major public health concern in developing countries, including India, where it is caused by the hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E viruses. Documenting the clinical profile and outcomes of hospitalized patients with AVH in a systematic way is important for guiding management decisions and informing public health strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective observational study carried out at the Department of Medicine and Gastroenterology, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital Ludhiana, over 12 months (May 2024 to May 2025). A total of 203 adults aged 18 years or older with serologically confirmed AVH were enrolled. Clinical features, biochemical parameters, complications, and outcomes, including discharge, death, and discharge against medical advice, were recorded. Data were analyzed using SPSS v26 with Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests; P < 0.05 was taken as statistically significant. RESULTS: The mean age was 26.1 ± 6.3 years, and males predominated at 75.4%. Hepatitis A virus (HAV) was the leading cause at 83.3%, followed by hepatitis E virus (HEV) at 8.4% and mixed HAV-HEV co-infection in another 8.4%. Jaundice (93.6%), nausea (86.7%), myalgia (77.3%), and fever (69.5%) were the most common presenting symptoms. Acute liver failure (ALF) occurred in 27.6% of patients and was the most important predictor of outcome; all 11 deaths (5.4%) were confined to the ALF group. Hemolysis was found in 15.3% and was linked to significantly worse outcomes. In all, 89.7% of patients were discharged, 5.4% died, and 4.9% left against medical advice. CONCLUSION: HAV is now the dominant cause of hospitalized AVH in young adults in this region, reflecting a shift from the traditionally childhood-onset pattern. ALF is the critical determinant of mortality, and early identification of high-risk features such as encephalopathy, coagulopathy, hemolysis, and renal dysfunction is essential for timely intervention. Hepatitis A vaccination and improvements in water safety and sanitation are urgently needed.

title: Predictive factors of virological response to direct-acting antivirals in patients with HBV/HCV coinfection
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B and C virus (HBV/HCV) coinfection complicates antiviral management, and predictors of direct-acting antiviral non-response remain insufficiently characterized in endemic settings. This study evaluated baseline clinical, virological, and fibrosis-related predictors of early and sustained non-response after sofosbuvir- and daclatasvir-based therapy. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, 207 adults with HBV/HCV coinfection treated at Holy Family Hospital, Rawalpindi, Pakistan, received 12 weeks of sofosbuvir and daclatasvir. SVR4 and SVR12 failure were defined as detectable HCV RNA levels at 4 and 12 weeks after treatment completion. Predictors were measured before treatment initiation. Univariable screening, exploratory multivariate logistic regression, and internally validated machine learning models were applied separately for SVR4 and SVR12 failure. Performance was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, AUROC, PR-AUC, and SHAP importance. Results SVR4 was achieved by 186 patients (89.9%), whereas 21 (10.1%) had SVR4 failure. SVR12 was achieved by 175 patients (84.5%), whereas 32 (15.5%) had SVR12 failure. In multivariable models, SVR4 failure was associated with a higher BMI, higher baseline HCV RNA levels, and male sex; IFN-regimen status was associated with a lower adjusted odds of failure. SVR12 failure was associated with older age, higher BMI, male sex, and higher baseline HCV RNA levels; IFN-regimen status again showed lower adjusted odds. XGBoost showed the highest SVR4 PR-AUC, whereas Random Forest showed the highest SVR12 PR-AUC. SHAP identified HCV RNA levels, age, BMI, and fibrosis indices as key contributors. Conclusions DAA therapy achieved high SVR rates in HBV/HCV coinfection. Baseline host and viral variables informed failure prediction; while fibrosis-related variables contributed at the descriptive and model interpretation level; however, the models remain exploratory and require external validation.

title: Liver transplantation outcomes, systemic immune–inflammatory phenotype, and predictors of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence in an HBV/HDV-endemic region: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B and D virus (HBV/HDV) coinfection sustains a hepatic inflammatory microenvironment from which hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises. Although advances in liver transplantation have improved survival, HCC recurrence remains a major challenge affecting long-term outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate post-transplant outcomes and identify risk factors associated with HCC recurrence among liver transplant recipients in Mongolia, and to characterize their pre-transplant systemic immune–inflammatory phenotype. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 146 patients with HCC who underwent liver transplantation at the National Cancer Center of Mongolia from 2018 through February 2026. Survival was estimated using Kaplan–Meier analysis with the log-rank test, and factors associated with HCC recurrence were assessed using univariable Cox regression. Pre-transplant neutrophil (ANC) and lymphocyte (ALC) counts and their ratio (NLR) were available for 139 recipients; lymphopenia was an ALC below 1.0 ×10 9 /L. The 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival rates were 88.7%, 82.1%, and 80.5%, respectively, with no significant difference between patients within versus beyond the Milan criteria (p = 0.097). HCC recurrence occurred in 3.4% of recipients and was significantly more common among patients beyond the Milan criteria (p = 0.001). Macrovascular invasion (HR, 12.76; p = 0.005), beyond-Milan status (HR, 10.04; p = 0.039), higher Edmondson–Steiner grade (HR, 9.25; p = 0.047), and elevated AFP (HR, 15.95; p = 0.003) were associated with recurrence in univariate analysis. HCV/HBV/HDV coinfection was significantly associated with higher post-transplant mortality. Median NLR was 1.84 and 39.6% of recipients were lymphopenic; NLR varied inversely with the ALC (ρ = −0.61) and positively with the ANC (ρ = +0.67, both p < 0.001). Lymphopenia increased with tumor burden (34.4% within Milan, 51.2% beyond, 3 of 5 recurrences), NLR was higher when HCC was histologically confirmed on the explant (2.10 vs 1.44, p = 0.015), and recurrence deaths showed the highest NLR with the lowest ALC, rejection deaths the reverse. Liver transplantation achieved favorable survival outcomes in patients with HCC in Mongolia. In exploratory univariate analysis, incorporating pre-transplant tumor characteristics, biomarkers, and viral etiology, together with the pre-transplant lymphocyte compartment, may improve prediction of recurrence and post-transplant mortality, particularly among patients beyond the Milan criteria.

title: Kinesin motor proteins as host factors regulating viral infection: Mechanisms of exploitation, emerging paradigms, and therapeutic horizons.
abstract: Intracellular transport via microtubules is integral to eukaryotic cell function, and viruses have developed intricate mechanisms to exploit this system at nearly every stage of their replication cycle. The mammalian kinesin superfamily, consisting of 14 distinct families, enables anterograde transport that is used by both DNA and RNA viruses. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of how a wide range of viral pathogens-including herpesviruses, human immunodeficiency virus type 1, vaccinia virus, hepatitis B virus (HBV), influenza virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-interact with specific kinesin family members to promote viral entry, genome trafficking, organization of replication compartments, assembly, and egress. Recent findings underscore the role of the kinesin-4 family member KIF4A as a novel host factor for HBV. The therapeutic potential of modulating the surface expression of the HBV-entry receptor (NTCP) is discussed, either by suppressing KIF4 expression-necessary for anti-retrograde transport of NTCP to the cell surface-or by disrupting the NTCP-KIF4 interaction. Additionally, emerging pharmacological approaches targeting kinesin-dependent transport are evaluated. By establishing a unified framework that connects motor protein biology to virology, this review identifies key knowledge gaps and outlines future research directions for the development of broad-spectrum, host-targeted, antiviral therapies.

title: Enfermedades inmunoprevalentes y la importancia de la vacunación en la salud comunitaria.
abstract: Vaccine preventable diseases are an issue, for public health. Even though we have effective vaccines people are still getting sick and having outbreaks. This is especially true for people who're vulnerable. Getting vaccinated is one of the ways to stop infectious diseases from spreading and it helps reduce the number of people who die from these diseases. It also helps keep our communities healthy. However not as many people are getting vaccinated as they used to. This is because of things like social and economic problems, lack of education and people believing false information. This makes it easier for diseases that we thought were under control to come back. The main goal of this research is to look at the vaccine preventable diseases and how important vaccination is for keeping our communities healthy. To do this we looked at a lot of articles that were published between 2021 and 2026. We searched databases like SciELO, PubMed and Google Scholar. We only looked at articles that met criteria. What we found out is that diseases like measles, rubella and mumps are still problems. We also found out that diseases like diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus and poliomyelitis are still around. Then there are diseases like influenza, hepatitis B and rotavirus. When a lot of people get vaccinated it really helps reduce the number of cases, hospitalizations and outbreaks. This also helps keep our communities healthy. So vaccine preventable diseases are still a problem, around the world. We know that getting vaccinated is the best way to stop these diseases. We need to make sure that people get vaccinated on time and that we keep vaccinating them. This is why it is so important to have immunization programs and to educate our communities.

To do this we looked at a lot of articles that were published between 2021 and 2026. We searched databases like SciELO, PubMed and Google Scholar. We only looked at articles that met criteria. What we found out is that diseases like measles, rubella and mumps are still problems. We also found out that diseases like diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus and poliomyelitis are still around. Then there are diseases like influenza, hepatitis B and rotavirus. When a lot of people get vaccinated it really helps reduce the number of cases, hospitalizations and outbreaks. This also helps keep our communities healthy. So vaccine preventable diseases are still a problem, around the world. We know that getting vaccinated is the best way to stop these diseases. We need to make sure that people get vaccinated on time and that we keep vaccinating them. This is why it is so important to have immunization programs and to educate our communities.

title: KHẢO SÁT TÌNH TRẠNG NHIỄM HBV THỂ ẨN VÀ HBV GIAI ĐOẠN CỬA SỔ Ở NGƯỜI HIẾN MÁU TẠI VIỆN HUYẾT HỌC - TRUYỀN MÁU TRUNG ƯƠNG NĂM 2025-2026
abstract: Mặc dù xét nghiệm HBsAg được áp dụng thường quy, nhiễm HBV giai đoạn cửa sổ và thể ẩn (Occult HBV Infection - OBI) vẫn tiềm ẩn nguy cơ lây qua đường truyền máu. Bổ sung xét nghiệm khuếch đại acid nucleic (NAT) là giải pháp then chốt nâng cao an toàn truyền máu. Mục tiêu: Xác định tỷ lệ nhiễm HBV và đánh giá hiệu quả của NAT trong sàng lọc HBV thể ẩn và giai đoạn cửa sổ tại Viện Huyết học – Truyền máu Trung ương. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu hồi cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên 668.576 đơn vị máu hiến từ tháng 04/2025 đến 03/2026. Mẫu máu được sàng lọc HBsAg (điện hóa phát quang/hóa phát quang) và HBV-DNA (kỹ thuật NAT). Các mẫu NAT yield được phân loại WP và OBI bằng xét nghiệm anti-HBc IgM, anti-HBc II và anti-HBs. Kết quả: Tỷ lệ HBsAg dương tính là 0,206% (1.380/668.576). NAT phát hiện thêm 328 ca HBV-DNA dương tính đơn độc (tỷ lệ 0,049%, tương đương 1/2.038 mẫu HBsAg âm tính), nâng hiệu suất phát hiện HBV thêm 23,7%. Nguy cơ nhiễm tăng dần theo tuổi, cao nhất ở nhóm 46–60 tuổi (OR = 3,390; 95%CI: 2,947–3,899). Người hiến máu nhắc lại có nguy cơ nhiễm thấp hơn có ý nghĩa so với hiến lần đầu (OR = 0,106; 95%CI: 0,095–0,117). Trong 230 ca NAT yield được làm xét nghiệm bổ sung, OBI chiếm 93,04% (214/230) và WP chiếm 6,96% (16/230). Kết luận: NAT giúp phát hiện đáng kể các ca nhiễm HBV giai đoạn cửa sổ và thể ẩn bị bỏ sót bởi xét nghiệm huyết thanh học, khẳng định giá trị bắt buộc của xét nghiệm này trong bảo đảm an toàn truyền máu tại Việt Nam.

source_records.abstract: Mặc dù xét nghiệm HBsAg được áp dụng thường quy, nhiễm HBV giai đoạn cửa sổ và thể ẩn (Occult HBV Infection - OBI) vẫn tiềm ẩn nguy cơ lây qua đường truyền máu. Bổ sung xét nghiệm khuếch đại acid nucleic (NAT) là giải pháp then chốt nâng cao an toàn truyền máu. Mục tiêu: Xác định tỷ lệ nhiễm HBV và đánh giá hiệu quả của NAT trong sàng lọc HBV thể ẩn và giai đoạn cửa sổ tại Viện Huyết học – Truyền máu Trung ương. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu hồi cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên 668.576 đơn vị máu hiến từ tháng 04/2025 đến 03/2026. Mẫu máu được sàng lọc HBsAg (điện hóa phát quang/hóa phát quang) và HBV-DNA (kỹ thuật NAT). Các mẫu NAT yield được phân loại WP và OBI bằng xét nghiệm anti-HBc IgM, anti-HBc II và anti-HBs. Kết quả: Tỷ lệ HBsAg dương tính là 0,206% (1.380/668.576). NAT phát hiện thêm 328 ca HBV-DNA dương tính đơn độc (tỷ lệ 0,049%, tương đương 1/2.038 mẫu HBsAg âm tính), nâng hiệu suất phát hiện HBV thêm 23,7%. Nguy cơ nhiễm tăng dần theo tuổi, cao nhất ở nhóm 46–60 tuổi (OR = 3,390; 95%CI: 2,947–3,899). Người hiến máu nhắc lại có nguy cơ nhiễm thấp hơn có ý nghĩa so với hiến lần đầu (OR = 0,106; 95%CI: 0,095–0,117). Trong 230 ca NAT yield được làm xét nghiệm bổ sung, OBI chiếm 93,04% (214/230) và WP chiếm 6,96% (16/230). Kết luận: NAT giúp phát hiện đáng kể các ca nhiễm HBV giai đoạn cửa sổ và thể ẩn bị bỏ sót bởi xét nghiệm huyết thanh học, khẳng định giá trị bắt buộc của xét nghiệm này trong bảo đảm an toàn truyền máu tại Việt Nam.

title: Associations Between Self‐Reported Previous Hepatitis C Diagnosis, Hepatitis C Treatment, and Current Binge Drinking Among Persons Who Inject Drugs—National HIV Behavioural Surveillance, 2015–2024
abstract: ABSTRACT Persons who inject drugs (PWID) are disproportionately affected by hepatitis C virus (HCV). Excessive alcohol use among PWID can lead to more rapid progression of liver disease among persons with HCV. We assessed associations between ever reporting HCV infection, ever reporting HCV treatment, and current binge drinking among PWID who participated in National HIV Behavioural Surveillance (NHBS) during 2015–2024. NHBS conducted biobehavioural surveys among PWID using respondent‐driven sampling in 2015, 2018, 2022, and 2024. We estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the association between self‐report of ever having HCV infection, HCV treatment, and binge drinking in the past 30 days. The percentage of PWID reporting binge drinking was 25.8% in 2015, 24.0% in 2018, 13.3% in 2022, and 17.2% in 2024. In adjusted analysis, we found a significant negative relationship between self‐reported ever having HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days in three of the four surveys: 2018 (aPR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83–0.99), 2022 (aPR: 0.79, 95% CI:0.70–0.90), and 2024 (aPR:0.78, 95% CI: 0.65–0.93). We did not find significant associations between previously ever receiving treatment for HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days across the four survey years. Among PWID, HCV infection was associated with reduced prevalence of binge drinking in 2018, 2022, and 2024. Our results support the importance of testing PWID for HCV infection and continued education on the harms associated with excessive alcohol use, including among persons who have received treatment for HCV infection.

title: Sustained HBsAg seroclearance after pembrolizumab-containing neoadjuvant therapy in a patient with synchronous esophageal and gastric cancer: a case report
abstract: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has been described in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but evidence outside HCC remains limited and requires further validation. We report a patient with synchronous early-stage esophageal cancer and locally advanced gastric cancer who achieved HBsAg seroclearance after three cycles of pembrolizumab containing neoadjuvant therapy. Before treatment, qHBsAg was detectable at a low level (0.41 IU/mL), whereas HBV DNA was below the assay lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) (<30 IU/mL). HBsAg first became nonreactive on July 20, 2022 and remained below the assay cutoff on subsequent measurements. At the most recent follow-up on September 10, 2026, qHBsAg remained below the cutoff (<0.05 IU/mL) and HBV DNA remained below the LLOQ, with normal liver biochemistry. Notably, the patient did not receive antiviral therapy during treatment and remained free from both tumor recurrence and HBV reactivation for more than four years after surgery. This case raises the possibility that ICIs may confer concurrent antitumor and assisting antiviral effects in selected HBsAg-positive patients with cancer. However, given the single-case design, the extremely low baseline HBsAg level, and concomitant multimodal anticancer therapy, a causal relationship between pembrolizumab and HBsAg loss cannot be established. Further studies are warranted to clarify whether ICIs can contribute to HBV immune control, particularly when integrated with current antiviral strategies.

title: Evaluation of the Bosphore HBV Quantification Kit: Categorical and Quantitative Agreement with the Aptima HBV Quant Assay for HBV DNA Detection and Quantification
abstract: Accurate hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA quantification is essential for assessing viral replication and monitoring antiviral therapy. This retrospective method-comparison study evaluated the Bosphore HBV Quantification Kit against the Aptima HBV Quant Assay using 130 residual anonymized EDTA-plasma specimens, comprising 110 comparator-positive and 20 comparator-negative samples. Categorical agreement was assessed using positive, negative, and overall percent agreement (PPA, NPA, and OPA), while quantitative agreement was evaluated using a predefined ±0.5 log10 IU/mL criterion, Bland–Altman analysis, Passing–Bablok regression, and Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). PPA was 100% (110/110; 95% confidence interval [CI], 96.70–100.00%), NPA was 95.0% (19/20; 95% CI, 75.13–99.87%), and OPA was 99.23% (129/130; 95% CI, 95.79–99.98%). One confirmed qualitative discordance was observed. Overall, 109/110 paired numerical results (99.1%; 95% CI, 95.04–99.98%) were within ±0.5 log10 IU/mL. Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +0.124 log10 IU/mL, Passing–Bablok regression yielded Y = 0.107 + 1.019X, and Lin’s CCC was 0.991. The Bosphore assay demonstrated high categorical and quantitative agreement with the comparator across the HBV DNA concentration range evaluated, supporting its potential suitability for quantitative HBV DNA testing within the analytical workflow assessed in this study.
