title: Trends in hepatitis C treatment initiation alongside changes in Medicaid policy requirements: Wisconsin, January 2015-December 2022.
abstract: Background Treatment is recommended for all persons with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, which substantially reduces HCV-associated morbidity and mortality. A US state Medicaid program incrementally removed policies restricting access to direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, including specialist and severity requirements (2017), sobriety (2019), and prior authorization (2020). We evaluated longitudinal trends in hepatitis C treatment initiation alongside the timing of these policy changes. Objective To describe HCV treatment initiation rates concurrently with the removal of restrictive policies among a population of Medicaid recipients with recently diagnosed infection. Methods We matched public health surveillance data and Medicaid claims to identify Medicaid recipients with HCV infection during January 2015-December 2022. We defined treatment initiation as at least 1 pharmacy claim for DAAs within 6 months of hepatitis C diagnosis among persons with 6-month continuous Medicaid enrollment. We evaluated longitudinal changes in treatment rates across distinct policy periods using modified Poisson regression models adjusted for sex, race, ethnicity, and birthyear cohort. Adjusted rate ratios and 95% CIs were calculated. Results Yearly treatment ranged from 1% (among those diagnosed in 2015) to a maximum of 23% (among those diagnosed in 2020). In the multivariable model evaluating trends concurrent with policy changes, treatment initiation was 2.8 times (95% CI = 2.2-3.6) as high as baseline during the period without specialist provider and disease severity restrictions; 3.7 times (95% CI = 2.8-4.8) as high during the period without sobriety restrictions; and 5.6 times (95% CI = 4.4-7.0) as high during the period when all administrative restrictions were absent. Conclusions Overall treatment uptake remained low in this population of Medicaid beneficiaries diagnosed with hepatitis C, despite the incremental removal of policy requirements. Although relative treatment rates increased across successive policy periods, initiation peaked at just 23%. These findings suggest that although removing administrative barriers is a necessary baseline step, policy liberalization alone is insufficient to achieve hepatitis C elimination, and additional clinical and structural interventions are needed.

title: Anti-HBc seropositivity among women of childbearing age in Indonesia: a nationally representative cross-sectional study
abstract: Objective This study aimed to estimate the national prevalence of hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) seropositivity, indicating prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure, among Indonesian women aged 15–49 years. Additionally, the study sought to identify associated sociodemographic factors. Methods We analyzed data from the 2018 Indonesian Basic Health Survey (Riskesdas), a nationally representative survey with a complex sampling design and appropriate sampling weights. Anti-HBc seropositivity was measured at the Sulianti Saroso Laboratory. Of the 19,418 participants, 12,617 women were included in the final analysis. Survey-weighted logistic regression was applied to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORaj) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Anti-HBc seropositivity was significantly more common among women aged >35 years (ORaj = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.58–1.87), those with lower educational attainment (ORaj = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.05–1.28), employed women (ORaj = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.09–1.29), rural residents (ORaj = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.18–1.40), and women reporting contraceptive use (ORaj = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.11–1.35). Conclusion Anti-HBc seropositivity remains a significant public health concern among Indonesian women of childbearing age, particularly those who are older, less educated, employed, living in rural areas, and reporting contraceptive use. Policy recommendations should prioritize maternal screening, timely and universal birth dose vaccination, administration of hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) when indicated, and improved vaccination coverage among unvaccinated adults.

title: Application Research on mRNA Vaccine Technology in Infectious Disease Prevention and Control
abstract: Compared with inactivated, subunit, and DNA nucleic-acid approaches, mRNA vaccines do not enter the nucleus and carry no risk of genomic integration; they are translated in the cytoplasm and can jointly induce humoral and cellular immunity. In vitro transcription and cell-free production also markedly shorten the interval from sequence acquisition to vaccine output. This paper summarizes the configurations of non-replicating, self-amplifying, and circular RNA vaccines, as well as the characteristics of PRR-mediated immune activation, and reviews key process technologies including the 5′ cap, UTRs, pseudouridine modification, dsRNA removal, and LNP delivery. At the application level, the discussion centers on the billion-scale administration of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines, booster immunization, and variant-component updating, while also reviewing progress and limitations in pipelines for influenza, rabies post-exposure prophylaxis, HIV, hepatitis B, and other diseases, and analyzing their public health significance in shortening emergency response windows and tracking strain drift. IVT purity, ultracold-chain requirements, and accessibility in resource-limited regions remain the main constraints. Self-amplifying/circular RNA, multivalent combination vaccines, and inhalable mucosal delivery may help move this platform from a “single pandemic response” toward broader infectious disease prevention and control practice.

title: Identification of gastroesophageal varices in patients with cirrhosis using a CatBoost model derived From routine laboratory parameters
abstract: Objective To construct and internally validate a machine learning-assisted diagnostic model that identifies gastroesophageal varices (GEV) in patients with cirrhosis from routinely collected clinical and laboratory data. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 5,037 patients with cirrhosis who underwent endoscopy from January 2024 through May 2026. Random allocation at a 7:3 ratio produced a training set ( n = 3,526) and a validation set ( n = 1,511). Candidate features were reduced using multivariable logistic regression and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Ten machine learning algorithms were trained. Selection of the final model incorporated validation-set discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and the difference in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) between the training and validation sets. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantified the contribution of each feature. CatBoost was evaluated against the albumin–platelet product (APP), fibrosis index (FI), a univariable platelet count (PLT) model, and the Lok index in the validation cohort. Exploratory analyses examined performance within subgroups defined by age, sex, hepatitis B virus (HBV) etiology, and ascites. This is a model for adjunct recognition of existing GEV, not a rule for deferring endoscopy. Results GEV was documented endoscopically in 3,320 patients (65.91%). CatBoost yielded an AUROC of 0.865 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.845–0.884) in the validation set; accuracy was 0.811, sensitivity was 0.897, specificity was 0.647, and the Brier score was 0.135 (95% CI, 0.125–0.146). The AUROC decrease from training to validation was 0.038 for CatBoost and 0.051 for XGBoost. Albumin, red cell distribution width, and platelet count contributed most strongly to the CatBoost output in SHAP analysis. The AUROC for CatBoost (0.865) exceeded those for FI (0.796), APP (0.728), the PLT model (0.662), and the Lok index (0.592); each paired DeLong comparison remained significant after Holm adjustment (all P < 0.001). Across eight exploratory subgroups, AUROCs varied from 0.833 to 0.879. Conclusion A CatBoost classifier incorporating 10 routine laboratory variables demonstrated good discrimination and calibration during internal validation and provided higher net benefit than the four conventional comparators across most evaluated thresholds. It may provide adjunctive information before endoscopy; prospective evaluation and multicenter external validation remain necessary before clinical decision use.

title: Reductions in Advanced Chronic Liver Disease Among People Who Inject Drugs: The ETHOS Engage Study.
abstract: Background and aims Liver disease is a significant risk for people who inject drugs due to the high burden of hepatitis C virus (HCV). There is limited data on the impact of the direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy era on liver disease among people who inject drugs. This study evaluated baseline and longitudinal liver disease in a national cohort of people who inject drugs recruited over three Waves: 2018-2019, 2019-2021, and 2023-2025. Methods The ETHOS Engage Study is an observational cohort of people who inject drugs attending drug treatment clinics and needle and syringe programs in Australia. Participants completed a questionnaire and underwent point-of-care HCV RNA testing (Xpert HCV Viral Load Fingerstick) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by vibration-controlled transient hepatic elastography (FibroScan). Advanced chronic liver disease was defined by LSM of 10 kPa or above. Results Among all enrolments with a valid LSM (n = 3126, 79% recruited at drug treatment clinics), 11% had advanced chronic liver disease, decreasing from 12.0% (154/1287) in 2018-2019 to 7.9% (66/839) in 2019-2021, and 6.4% (62/967) in 2023-2025. In adjusted analyses, participants recruited between 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 were less likely to have advanced chronic liver disease (vs. 2018-2019; aOR 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.90 and aOR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.40-0.77, respectively). Current HCV infection declined from 24% in 2018-2019 to 10% in 2023-2025. Among participants with LSM in more than one wave and current HCV infection at first visit and no current HCV infection at second visit (n = 44), advanced chronic liver disease declined from 19% to 5%. Conclusions Unrestricted access to DAA therapies in Australia has been associated with reduced liver disease burden among people who inject drugs. Monitoring of liver health in this population is important, given potential ageing and non-HCV liver disease impacts.

title: GAMBARAN INSIDENSI HBSAG PADA IBU HAMIL DI PUSKESMAS TULANGAN SIDOARJO
abstract: Hepatitis B in pregnant women requires attention because infection with the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) can be transmitted from mother to infant and may develop into chronic infection. Therefore, Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) screening during antenatal care (ANC) is important for early detection and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission. This study aimed to determine the incidence of HBsAg among pregnant women at Tulangan Community Health Center, Sidoarjo, and describe respondents’ characteristics according to age, gestational age, and gravidity. A descriptive study design with purposive sampling was employed, involving 38 pregnant women from a population of 60 women attending ANC services between March and April 2026. HBsAg screening was performed using an immunochromatographic rapid test. Data were analyzed descriptively and presented as frequency distributions and percentages. The results showed that 1 respondent (2.6%) tested reactive for HBsAg, while 37 respondents (97.4%) tested non-reactive. The reactive case occurred in a woman aged 26–35 years, in the second trimester, and classified as secundigravida. In conclusion, the proportion of reactive HBsAg results among the respondents was 2.6%. Routine HBsAg screening during pregnancy is important to support early detection and prevent mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B. ABSTRAK Hepatitis B pada ibu hamil perlu mendapat perhatian karena infeksi virus hepatitis B (Hepatitis B Virus/HBV) dapat ditularkan dari ibu kepada bayi dan berisiko berkembang menjadi infeksi kronis. Oleh karena itu, pemeriksaan Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) melalui pelayanan antenatal care (ANC) penting dilakukan untuk mendukung deteksi dini dan pencegahan penularan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui insidensi HBsAg pada ibu hamil di Puskesmas Tulangan, Sidoarjo, serta menggambarkan karakteristik responden berdasarkan umur, umur kehamilan, dan paritas. Penelitian menggunakan desain deskriptif dengan teknik purposive sampling terhadap 38 ibu hamil dari populasi 60 ibu hamil yang menjalani pemeriksaan ANC pada Maret–April 2026. Pemeriksaan HBsAg dilakukan menggunakan metode imunokromatografi dengan rapid test. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif dan disajikan dalam bentuk distribusi frekuensi serta persentase. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa 1 responden (2,6%) memiliki hasil HBsAg reaktif, sedangkan 37 responden (97,4%) nonreaktif. Kasus reaktif ditemukan pada kelompok umur 26–35 tahun, trimester II, dan secundigravida. Disimpulkan bahwa proporsi hasil HBsAg reaktif pada responden yang diteliti sebesar 2,6%. Pemeriksaan HBsAg secara rutin diperlukan untuk mendukung deteksi dini dan pencegahan penularan hepatitis B dari ibu kepada bayi.

Penelitian menggunakan desain deskriptif dengan teknik purposive sampling terhadap 38 ibu hamil dari populasi 60 ibu hamil yang menjalani pemeriksaan ANC pada Maret–April 2026. Pemeriksaan HBsAg dilakukan menggunakan metode imunokromatografi dengan rapid test. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif dan disajikan dalam bentuk distribusi frekuensi serta persentase. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa 1 responden (2,6%) memiliki hasil HBsAg reaktif, sedangkan 37 responden (97,4%) nonreaktif. Kasus reaktif ditemukan pada kelompok umur 26–35 tahun, trimester II, dan secundigravida. Disimpulkan bahwa proporsi hasil HBsAg reaktif pada responden yang diteliti sebesar 2,6%. Pemeriksaan HBsAg secara rutin diperlukan untuk mendukung deteksi dini dan pencegahan penularan hepatitis B dari ibu kepada bayi.

source_records.abstract: Hepatitis B in pregnant women requires attention because infection with the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) can be transmitted from mother to infant and may develop into chronic infection. This study aimed to determine the incidence of HBsAg among pregnant women at Tulangan Community Health Center, Sidoarjo, and describe respondents’ characteristics according to age, gestational age, and gravidity. The reactive case occurred in a woman aged 26–35 years, in the second trimester, and classified as secundigravida. In conclusion, the proportion of reactive HBsAg results among the respondents was 2.6%. Routine HBsAg screening during pregnancy is important to support early detection and prevent mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B. title: Pulmonary and Extra-Pulmonary Tuberculosis Burden in Southern Libya: A Five-Year Epidemiological Survey at Sebha Medical Center
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a significant public health challenge affecting both pulmonary and extrapulmonary systems. This study investigated the clinical distribution and demographic patterns of TB among hospitalized patients at Sebha Medical Center, highlighting the infection burden in Sebha and its surrounding regions. Methods: A descriptive, cross-sectional, laboratory- and radiology-based epidemiological survey was conducted from 2022 to August 2026. The study evaluated 152 confirmed TB cases admitted to Sebha Medical Center. Results: Out of 152 patients enrolled, 61.8% presented with pulmonary TB and 19.1% with extrapulmonary TB. Young adults aged 20-35 years constituted the most frequently affected group, accounting for 48.0%. A significant male predominance was observed among notified TB cases, indicating a marked gender disparity. Out of 142 known nationalities, Libyan nationality accounted for 47.4% of cases. High clusters were concentrated in Sebha city. Among the extra-pulmonary manifestations, abdominal/lymph node TB was the most prevalent site (24.1%). Coinfection with HIV/AIDS, HBV and HCV was also documented in this study. Conclusion: Tuberculosis is a critical threat in southern Libya, primarily affecting the working-age population. Driven by migration and social mobility, the disease is overwhelmingly pulmonary, posing a severe risk for airborne community transmission. This highlights an urgent need for enhanced screening, robust surveillance, and targeted public health interventions in Sebha.

title: Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Sofosbuvir-Based Therapy in Chinese Children and Adolescents With Chronic HCV Infection: A Retrospective Multicentre Study.
abstract: Few direct-acting antiviral regimens are approved in China for children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and data are limited on their efficacy and safety in this population. This retrospective, multi-centre study aimed to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (LDV/SOF) and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) in Chinese paediatric patients. The study included patients aged 3-17 years from five hospitals across China who received either LDV/SOF or SOF/VEL for chronic HCV infection. The outcomes included the proportion of patients who achieved sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12), normalisation rates of ALT and AST levels, and incidence of adverse events (AEs). A total of 129 patients from five sites were included and 128 completed 12 weeks of post-treatment follow-up. Mean age was 9.9 years (standard deviation, 3.9), with 30 (23.3%), 55 (42.6%), and 44 (34.1%) patients aged 3-6, 7-11, and 12-17 years, respectively, 84 (65.1%) were male, 62 (48.1%) were infected with genotype 3, and baseline ALT and AST levels were elevated in 64 (49.6%) and 75 (58.1%) patients, respectively. The SVR12 rate was 98.4% (126/128) in the overall population, remaining consistent across subgroups by sex, age, HCV genotype, or regimen. ALT and AST levels were normalised in all patients with available data. AEs were reported by 16.4% (21/128) of patients and none were serious. Collectively, this study demonstrated that LDV/SOF and SOF/VEL were highly effective and well tolerated in Chinese paediatric patients with chronic HCV infection.

title: Pemeriksaan HBsAG Menggunakan Metode Imunokromatografi Pada Pemulung di TPA Sekitar Lowok Waru Kota Malang
abstract: Waste pickers are among the occupational groups potentially exposed to biological hazards, including the hepatitis B virus (HBV), due to contact with waste materials and sharp objects in their working environment. This study aimed to describe the results of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) screening among waste pickers at three waste disposal sites in Malang City. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed involving 15 male waste pickers from Candi Panggung, Tlogomas, and Merjosari waste disposal sites, selected through purposive sampling. HBsAg screening was performed using capillary blood specimens with the immunochromatographic rapid test (ICT) method. The collected data were analyzed descriptively using frequency distributions and percentages. The results showed that the largest proportion of respondents was aged 40–50 years (33%), and all respondents (100%) had worked as waste pickers for more than five years. HBsAg screening identified 12 respondents (80%) with non-reactive results and 3 respondents (20%) with reactive results. These findings indicate the presence of reactive HBsAg screening results among the participants; however, further laboratory examinations are required to confirm their hepatitis B infection status. Due to the limited sample size and descriptive research design, the findings cannot establish the source of infection or a causal relationship between occupational exposure and HBV transmission. This study highlights the importance of occupational health education, appropriate personal protective equipment, and access to follow-up healthcare services for waste pickers.

title: Crowder-specific modulation of hepatitis C virus NS3/4A protease activity and local structural dynamics.
abstract: Macromolecular crowding modulates enzyme behavior in crowder- and protein-specific ways, yet its impact on viral proteases, which are often key therapeutic targets, remains unclear. Here, we investigated the hepatitis C virus NS3/4A protease under increasing concentrations of polyethylene glycols (PEGs), ficoll, dextran, and lysozyme using fluorescence-based assays to examine enzyme kinetics, local Trp environments, thermal stability, and rotational restriction of the fluorescent probe in the surrounding medium. PEGs reduced catalytic activity while leaving substrate binding either unaffected or slightly enhanced. These effects were accompanied by a moderate tryptophan fluorescence spectral narrowing, consistent with reduced heterogeneity in local conformational environments. In contrast, ficoll enhanced catalytic efficiency despite stronger fluorescence quenching, indicating local structural changes that favored catalysis. Dextran and lysozyme inhibited protease activity through distinct kinetic patterns, likely reflecting differences in their size, shape, and chemical properties. Thermal analysis revealed crowder-specific local structural changes in NS3/4A without global unfolding up to 65°C, with differences in local stability and flexibility corroborating the observed kinetic effects. Changes in the rotational restriction of the fluorescent probe further indicated that generalized restriction of molecular motion alone could not explain the effects of crowding on NS3/4A. These findings demonstrate that macromolecular crowding modulates NS3/4A catalysis through crowder-specific effects on local structure.

title: Timing of Earliest Documented Positive Hepatitis C Laboratory Result Relative to Delivery Among Pregnant Persons With Active Infection in West Virginia, 2022-2023.
abstract: Direct-acting antiviral therapy can cure hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection; however, because treatment is not recommended during pregnancy, preconception treatment remains the primary strategy to prevent perinatal HCV exposure. West Virginia birth records from 2022 to 2023 were linked with statewide HCV laboratory surveillance data. This linked dataset was used to identify births to persons with active HCV infection and characterize the timing of the earliest documented positive HCV laboratory result relative to delivery. A total of 426 deliveries resulting in 433 HCV-exposed live-born infants were identified. Most pregnant persons were aged 25-34 years, White and insured by Medicaid. Overall, 38.5% had their earliest documented positive HCV laboratory result more than 5 years prior to delivery, 36.9% had their first documented positive test 1-5 years prior to delivery and 24.6% had their first documented positive test within 1 year before delivery and up to 2 weeks postpartum. These findings indicate that many pregnant persons with active HCV infection had documented longstanding infection prior to pregnancy, highlighting opportunities to strengthen linkage to care and access to curative treatment before pregnancy.

title: Infectious disease screening rates among people who use drugs in open drug scenes: a brief report
abstract: Background and objectives People who use drugs (PWUD) face a high risk of infectious diseases. Brazil has one of the world’s largest crack-cocaine markets, with major cities struggling with public health challenges linked to open drug scenes (ODS), where illicit drugs are openly used and traded. Epidemiological data on screening rates and infection prevalence within ODS in Brazil remain scarce. This study examines the self-reported prevalence of screening tests for tuberculosis (TB), HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B (HBV), and C (HCV), as well as the factors influencing screening rates.Methods Three cross-sectional, self-report surveys of 900 PWUD in ODS in São Paulo between 2017 and 2022 were analysed.Results The majority of participants were male (68.26%), with a mean age of 36.89 years, and who frequented the ODS for five years or more (53.51%) Screening rates varied by disease, with the highest overall prevalence for HIV (63.59%) followed by TB (59.93%) and Syphilis (59.56%), HBV (50.22%) and HCV (48.94%). Across all infections, screening rates declined between 2017 and 2022. Factors associated with screening included age, gender, education, survey year, and lenght of time frequenting the ODS.Conclusion Findings highlight gaps in screening coverage. We advocate for a national serial bio-behavioral survey of PWUD in ODS to accurately assess screening prevalence, infection rates, and risk factors, which remain unmonitored.

title: Direct-Acting Antiviral Therapy in Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma Receiving Non-Curative Treatment: High Sustained Virological Response Rates and Preservation of Liver Functional Reserve.
abstract: Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) cure most chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections, but their impact on liver functional reserve in patients with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly after non-curative HCC treatment, remains unclear. We evaluated antiviral efficacy and liver functional reserve after DAA therapy according to HCC history and timing of DAA initiation. In this retrospective single-center cohort, 716 patients initiated DAA therapy, and 690 with evaluable sustained virological response at 12 weeks after treatment (SVR12) were analysed. Patients were classified as no HCC, curative-treated HCC, or non-curative-treated HCC according to the most recent HCC treatment before DAA initiation. Liver functional reserve was assessed using the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score, modified ALBI grade, and Child-Pugh class. In the non-curative-treated HCC group, early (≤ 3 months) versus delayed (> 3 months) DAA initiation after the most recent HCC treatment was compared. Overall SVR12 was 96.1%, with similarly high rates across groups regardless of HCC history. The median ALBI score improved from -2.35 to -2.58 at SVR12 in the curative-treated HCC group (p < 0.001) but remained unchanged in the non-curative-treated HCC group (-2.36 to -2.38). Among 64 patients with a history of HCC, 43 (67.2%) developed recurrence; in these patients, the ALBI score improved from -2.31 at DAA initiation to -2.57 at recurrence (p < 0.001), and more than 90% remained Child-Pugh class A. Early and delayed DAA initiation showed similarly high SVR12 rates and comparable liver functional reserve. DAAs achieved high SVR12 rates and maintained liver functional reserve in patients with HCV, including those with a history of HCC after non-curative treatment.

title: Ten-Year Structural Reversal of Severe Nodular Cirrhosis with Hepatic Atrophy in a Heavy Manual Laborer After Intermittent Neo-Chinese Medicine Treatment: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Reversing established cirrhosis with hepatic atrophy and severe nodularity is generally considered extremely difficult. We report a case of a heavy manual laborer with active, severe nodular cirrhosis and hepatic atrophy who achieved a decade-long structural reversal following intermittent Neo-Chinese Medicine treatment, avoiding decompensation. Case Presentation: A 61-year-old male farmer and bricklayer with a 10-year history of hepatitis B cirrhosis presented in February 2014 with mild ALT elevation (78.0 U/L) and abnormal liver fibrosis markers (hyaluronic acid 169 μg/L), indicating active cirrhosis. Baseline MRI revealed a shrunken liver with multiple nodular signals. Baseline FibroScan showed a liver stiffness of 25.2 kPa. Without timely intervention, rapid progression to decompensated cirrhosis was highly anticipated. He received intermittent Neo-Chinese Medicine treatment for 12 years while continuing heavy manual labor. His liver fibrosis markers normalized by the second follow-up. title: Case Report: Splenorenal shunt management after liver transplantation in a recipient with situs inversus totalis
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) alters graft positioning and vascular reconstruction during liver transplantation. A 56-year-old man with SIT, decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma received a 558-g deceased-donor whole-liver graft, with a graft-to-recipient weight ratio of 0.60%. The graft was implanted in the native left-sided hepatic fossa in a reversed orientation. Postoperative CT showed a large splenorenal shunt and heterogeneous graft enhancement. Portal vein velocity fell from 44.7 cm/s on postoperative day (POD) 1 to 25 cm/s on POD3–4 and was 32 cm/s on POD5. Endovascular occlusion was abandoned on POD5 because venography showed aneurysmal dilatation and the procedural risk was judged excessive. Open ligation of the approximately 3-cm shunt was performed on POD6, preserving the main renal vein. Portal vein velocity was 30 cm/s after ligation, 37 cm/s on POD7 and 42 cm/s on POD9. Total bilirubin decreased from 158.6 μmol/L on POD4 to 70.5 μmol/L on POD13; the international normalized ratio was 1.49 on POD6 and 1.02 on POD14. The patient was discharged on POD27. Imaging showed no tumor recurrence at approximately 19 months, and alpha-fetoprotein was 7.32 ng/mL at approximately 23 months. This case describes surgical treatment of suspected portal steal in an SIT recipient when endovascular shunt occlusion was unsuitable.

title: 23 Liquid biopsy insights: a plasma-based cell-free nucleic acid assay for simultaneous profiling of adaptive immune receptor repertoires, tumor gene expression, and oncoviral biomarkers
abstract: Background Immune repertoire profiling has conventionally required immune cells — PBMCs, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, or tissue biopsies — thereby limiting longitudinal immune monitoring studies in immuno-oncology. Cell-free nucleic acids (cfNA) isolated from plasma offer a minimally invasive alternative that captures complementary biological signals: cell-free DNA (cfDNA) released from dying cells undergoing apoptosis or necrosis, and cell-free RNA (cfRNA) enclosed within extracellular vesicles (EVs) from actively signaling immune and tumor cells. Together, cfDNA and cfRNA provide a dual snapshot of immune turnover and activation without the constraints of tissue collection. To leverage this, we developed an integrated plasma-based assay for parallel immune receptor, tumor gene expression, and viral biomarker profiling.Methods A specialized cfRNA + cfDNA co-purification kit was developed and optimized for high-yield, high-purity extraction from plasma, yielding a combined cfNA fraction compatible with all three downstream assays. (1) cfAIR TCR- /BCR-Seq: Targeted amplicon sequencing of T-cell receptor (TCR) and B-cell receptor (BCR) CDR3 regions from cfNA enables comprehensive immune repertoire profiling, with PBMC and FFPE tumor tissue samples used as specificity controls to identify plasma-enriched clonotypes associated with tumor-specific immune responses, treatment, or minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring. (2) cfEXP Targeted RNA-Seq: A focused panel of ~5,000 genes with low expression level in plasma cfRNA is designed for multiplex RT-PCR expression quantification of biomarkers for tumor subtyping, tissue-of-origin inference, and monitoring of therapy-induced transcriptional changes. (3) cfOncoVirus Profiling: Targeted profiling of 26 cancer-associated viral sequences in cfDNA and cfRNA enables detection of cancer-associated viral biomarkers — including EBV, HPV, HBV, and others — within the same workflow. All assays were validated using plasma samples from cancer patients and healthy donors, including samples from immunotherapy-treated cohorts.Results The cfAIR TCR-/BCR-Seq assay detected tumor-associated clonotypes in plasma that were confirmed by matched tissue sequencing, with plasma-specific clones enriched relative to PBMC controls ( figure 1). The cfEXP Targeted RNA-Seq assay identified cancer-type-specific gene expression signatures and tracked transcriptional shifts before and after treatment. The cfOncoVirus Profiling assay detected viral sequences consistent with known tumor-virus associations across multiple cancer types.Conclusions This integrated cfNA platform enables biopsy-free, multimodal profiling of adaptive immune receptor repertoires, tumor transcriptomes, and oncoviral biomarkers from a single plasma sample. By capturing both immune activation (cfRNA/EVs) and immune turnover (cfDNA), the platform is uniquely suited to translational immuno-oncology workflows, including treatment response monitoring, MRD surveillance, and immune biomarker discovery in checkpoint immunotherapy and cell therapy trials.Abstract 23 Figure 1TCR and BCR sequences detected for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), melanoma, and healthy samples from plasma (cfNA, PBMC and FFPE tissue) samples

title: Prevalence of seroconversion of hepatitis C virus among children with chronic kidney disease on regular hemodialysis
abstract: Abstract Introduction Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in hemodialysis patients. hepatitis C virus infection is one of the most common blood-borne infections in Egypt. Objective To detect the prevalence of HCV infection and seroconversion among all hemodialysis in Assiut University Children’s Hospital Dialysis unit (ACUH). Methodology This study was Ambispective study. A total of 70 patients were included; the retrospective component includes patients who received hemodialysis between January 2018 and September 2023. the prospective component, covering October 2023 to October 2025. The study is conducted at the Children’s Dialysis Unit at AUCH. Results HCV seroconversion occurred in 28 (40.0%) patients. Seroconversion was associated with longer hemodialysis duration, with a progressive decline in HCV-free survival as dialysis duration increased. In Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, hemodialysis duration was the only independent predictor of HCV seroconversion in both univariable (HR = 0.721, 95% CI: 0.588–0.882, p = 0.002) and multivariable analyses (adjusted HR = 0.479, 95% CI: 0.294–0.779, p = 0.003). No significant independent associations were observed for CVC duration, history of blood transfusion, hemodialysis outside AUCH, or vascular access type. The annual incidence of seroconversion declined from 10.6% in 2018 to 5.0% in 2023, with no new cases recorded in 2024 or 2025, coinciding with the implementation and reinforcement of infection control measures. Conclusion HCV seroconversion remains a significant concern among paediatric hemodialysis patients; however, the incidence markedly declined due to effective infection control measures.

title: Environmental determinants of hepatitis E seroprevalence in internally displaced populations: a geospatial study from Sudan.
abstract: Background Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a major cause of viral hepatitis in humanitarian and resource-limited settings. Internally displaced persons (IDPs) are especially vulnerable due to overcrowding and inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) conditions. However, spatial variation in HEV exposure within camps remains poorly characterized. The objective of the current study was to determine the seroprevalence, spatial distribution, and environmental correlates of HEV exposure among IDPs in Al-Azaza Camp, Blue Nile State, Sudan. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1078 IDPs from August to December 2021. Serum samples were tested for anti-HEV IgG and IgM using ELISA. Household environmental and behavioral data were collected through questionnaires and observation. GPS coordinates were mapped in ArcGIS Pro to assess spatial clustering. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of seropositivity. Results Overall HEV seroprevalence was 76.4%, with low IgM positivity (1.85%), suggesting limited recent transmission. Significant spatial clustering was observed, driven mainly by IgG-positive cases. Independent risk factors included proximity to open defecation sites, unsafe water storage, poor solid waste disposal, and animal husbandry. Conclusion HEV exposure was widespread and spatially clustered, reflecting cumulative transmission. Targeted, sustained improvements in WASH infrastructure are crucial to reduce ongoing risk among displaced populations.

title: Evidence of rat hepatitis E virus across human and swine populations in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract Background. Rocahepevirus ratti (rat hepatitis E virus, ratHEV) is an emerging zoonotic hepevirus maintained in rodents and increasingly recognized as a cause of acute and chronic hepatitis in humans. In Africa, available evidence is confined to rodent reservoirs and environmental matrices; neither human serological exposure nor infection of a domestic animal host has been documented. We conducted a cross-sectional study in southwestern Nigeria. Serum from 527 participants recruited into three cohorts with differing expected exposure (livestock-contact workers, rural villagers, students) was tested for ratHEV-specific IgG using a dot blot assay. Human sera were additionally screened for ratHEV RNA by multiplex real-time RT-PCR targeting two ORF1 regions. In parallel, 544 swine fecal samples from the same setting were screened by the same assay, with confirmatory nested PCR and sequencing. Cohort seroprevalences were compared and potential associations were estimated by Firth penalized logistic regression with profile penalized-likelihood intervals. RatHEV-specific IgG was detected in 15/527 participants (2.8%; 95% CI 1.7–4.6). Seropositivity was highest in the livestock-contact cohort (12/281; 4.3%; 95% CI 2.2–7.3), intermediate in students (2/79; 2.5%; 95% CI 0.3–8.9) and lowest in villagers (1/167; 0.6%; 95% CI 0.02–3.3). In the penalized model, livestock contact was associated with higher odds of seropositivity than village residence (OR 5.15; 95% CI 1.23–47.56; p = 0.022), whereas the student–villager contrast was not (OR 3.58; 95% CI 0.47–39.61; p = 0.212). No human serum pool was positive for ratHEV RNA. RatHEV RNA was detected in 4/544 swine fecal samples (0.7%; 95% CI 0.2–1.9). The four swine-derived sequences shared 98.3–99.7% nucleotide identity with each other and were assigned to genotype C1, subtype Ia, clustering with strains reported from a human case in France and from rodents in Sierra Leone. These findings extend African evidence on rat-associated hepeviruses from reservoir and environmental compartments to human serological exposure and molecular detection in domestic swine. The co-occurrence of human exposure and detection of ratHEV RNA in swine feces in a single setting supports integrated follow-up combining rodent, swine, environmental and clinically targeted human sampling in West Africa.

title: XRN1-dependent RNA homeostasis regulates hepatitis D virus
abstract: Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection causes the most severe form of viral hepatitis, yet the host mechanisms restricting HDV replication remain poorly understood. Although HDV infection activates the MDA5-LGP2 pathway and induces robust interferon (IFN) responses, these antiviral programs have limited impact on viral replication. Here we identify the 5’-3’ exoribonuclease XRN1 as a key regulator of HDV infection. Loss of XRN1 in hepatoma cells increased double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) levels and induced interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs), including MDA5 and MAVS, and limited HDV infection. XRN1 deficiency enhanced ADAR1-mediated RNA editing, revealing a dynamic interplay between endogenous dsRNA metabolism and antiviral sensing. Inhibition of type I IFN signaling restored MDA5 expression and rescued HDV replication in XRN1-deficient cells. To identify the downstream effectors responsible for this restriction, we combined transcriptomic profiling with functional siRNA screening and identified DUSP5 and SIRPA as previously unrecognized ISGs with anti-HDV activity. Together, our findings establish XRN1 as a gatekeeper of dsRNA homeostasis that controls HDV replication through innate immune activation and reveals host antiviral effectors that may provide therapeutic opportunities for chronic hepatitis D.

title: Seropositivity and trends of transfusion transmitted infections among blood donors at blood center of tertiary care hospital of Marathwada region, Maharashtra, India
abstract: Background: Blood transfusion is a life-saving intervention that has an essential role in patient management within health care system. The establishment of systems to ensure that all donated blood screened for transfusion -transmissible infections is a core component of every national blood programme. Testing for TTI’s before blood transfusion is crucial for safety of recipients. with each unit of blood, there is 1% chance of transfusion associated problems including TTI. The aim of this 5-year retrospective study was to analyze the trend of transfusion transmitted infections among blood donors to evaluate the seroprevalence of HIV, HBV, HCV, syphilis and malaria. Methods: A retrospective study was done at the blood center over a period of 5 years from January 2020 to December 2024 in healthy donors aged between 18-65 years. TTIs were performed using ELISA for HIV, HBV, HCV and HBsAg, peripheral blood smear for malaria and RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin) for syphilis. Results: Out of total 64603 healthy voluntary donors, prevalence of HIV, HBV, HCV, syphilis and malaria was (14) 0.021%, (257) 0.397%, (38) 0.058%, (12) 0.018% and 0 % respectively in our study. Conclusions: Implementation of strict donor selection criteria along with proper counselling of donors can help to decrease seroprevalence rate of transfusion transmitted diseases. Also, the prevalence rate can be useful for government and health administrative services to implement better policy for safe blood collection and transfusion.

title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a health system-wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum. METHODS: We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021-May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024-August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed. RESULTS: We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% (P=.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% (P<.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P=.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally. CONCLUSION: The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an important opportunity to initiate curative therapy.

title: Recommendations to Enhance Engagement in Perinatal Research With People Who Inject Drugs.
abstract: Women of reproductive age are significantly less likely than men to initiate hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, with the lowest uptake among women with children. Women who inject drugs who have children are a highly marginalised and stigmatised population who experience inequitable access to healthcare and poorer health outcomes. In the BUMP-C qualitative study-Bridging Unified Management of Pregnancy in hepatitis C care-we sought to investigate current HCV care pathways and perceptions of HCV management during pregnancy among women who inject drugs. During this study, several lessons emerged from both the challenges and successes in engaging with this population. The aim of this commentary is to outline key recommendations for optimally engaging women who inject drugs in perinatal research. These recommendations include building trust with research participants, promoting strategies for research flexibility and seeking and valuing community and lived experience. The voices of women who inject drugs, often neglected in this space, must be prioritised to improve health outcomes for them and their children.

title: Prevalelence and Factors Associated with Portal Hypertensive Gastropathy among Patients with Portal Hypertension
abstract: Introduction: Portal hypertensive gastropathy (PHG) is an under-recognized cause of morbidity in patients with portal hypertension (PH), with a reported prevalence of 20–80%. Portal hypertension and the severity of liver disease are the key predictors of PHG. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, severity, and associated risk factors of PHG in patients with PH. Methods: This observational study was conducted from August 2022 to December 2024 and enrolled subjects of any age and sex with clinical or laboratory evidence of PH, irrespective of etiology. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 27, with a p-value of ≤0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Among the participants (n = 128), 81 (63.5%) were male and 47 (36.5%) were female. The mean age was 51.45 ± 12.76 years, with no significant sex difference (p = 0.190). Most patients with cirrhotic PH (n=126, 98.4%) presented with features of decompensated cirrhosis: ascites in 61.7%, upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) in 28.9%, and hepatic encephalopathy in 23.4%. title: 138 Prospective phase 1 clinical development and optimization of the interferon-biased TLR7 agonist prodrug PRTX007
abstract: Background TLR7 agonists have long been proposed as combination partners for immune checkpoint inhibitors. We previously hypothesized that a clinically effective oral TLR7 agonist would preferentially activate plasmacytoid dendritic cells and elicit a preferential IRF7/interferon-biased pharmacodynamic response while minimizing systemic inflammation. 1 We thus designed the TLR7 agonist PRX034 which is systemically delivered by the oral prodrug PRTX007. As reported herein, PRX034 elicited a differentiated cellular pharmacodynamic profile when compared to other TLR7 agonists. This translated into the differentiated clinical pharmacology of PRTX007 as established in a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 1 study in healthy volunteers with drug administered on an every-other-day schedule (PRTX007-001).2–4 The results of the pharmacodynamic and dose schedule optimization in a second Phase 1 study (PRTX007-002, reported herein), informed the regimen currently under evaluation in the Phase 2 INFLECTION-003 (PRTX007-003) study.Methods Cellular pharmacology was established in human PBMCs from individual donors exposed to TLR7 (PRX034, PRX009, imiquimod) or TLR7/8 (resiquimod) agonists. In the PRTX007-002 clinical trial, soluble and transcriptional biomarker responses were characterized following optimized administration of PRTX007 using a distinct 3-days-on/4-days-off schedule in healthy volunteers.Results Structurally distinct TLR7 agonists elicited markedly distinct cytokine response profiles in human PBMCs ( figure 1). PRX034 demonstrated an interferon-biased profile while maintaining comparatively low levels of IL-6, TNFα and other inflammatory mediators. PRX009, a structurally related agonist, produced minimal IFNα and preferentially induced inflammatory cytokines (figure 2). Imiquimod generated lower IFNα than PRX034, while resiquimod exhibited an imiquimod-like profile with substantially greater inflammatory cytokine production at concentrations engaging TLR8 (not shown). Conventional TLR reporter assays did not predict these differentiated pharmacodynamic programs.Analysis of immune correlates from the PRTX007-002 study demonstrated robust induction of IFNα and downstream interferon response genes with limited induction of inflammatory cytokines, consistent with our human PBMC data and selective IRF7 mediated mechanism of action. Individual patient response magnitudes varied considerably; however, the temporal sequence of pathway activation and pharmacodynamic re-engagement following each cycle of dosing was highly reproducible across participants.Conclusions Primary human PBMC pharmacology revealed that PRTX007 induces a differentiated IRF7/interferon-biased response compared to other TLR7 agonists. Subsequent clinical optimization demonstrates that intermittent 3-days-on/4-days-off administration reproducibly amplified and re-engaged IFN responses while maintaining limited inflammatory cytokine induction. These studies demonstrate that structurally distinct TLR7 agonists can elicit fundamentally different cytokine responses and transcriptional programs and support the dose regimen of PRTX007 currently under evaluation in the Phase 2 INFLECTION-003 study.Trial Registration ANZCTR.ORG ACTRN12624000981527References Appleman J, Webber, S. PRTX007, an optimized TLR7 agonist for systemic immunotherapy of cancers: interim analysis of phase I study in healthy volunteers. 2022;82(12_Supplement):CT189.Lemech C, Argent C, Scribner C, Sharabi A, Daniels R, Appleman J. Activation of innate and adaptive immune response with a clinical stage TLR7 agonist prodrug PRTX007. 2023;83(8_Suppl):CT180.Lemech C, Argent C, Scribner C, Sharabi A, Daniels R, Appleman J. Clinical validation of an orally-delivered, systemically activated TLR7 agonist to boost host immune response to chronic viral diseases, including hepatitis B virus. Hepatology 2023;78(S1):1463-C.Ethics Approval ALFRED HREC: 110229/Alfred-2024.Abstract 138 Figure 1Primary human PBMC pharmacology identifies a differentiated interferon-biased pharmacodynamic profile supporting selection of PRTX007 for clinical development. Human PBMCs were incubated with PRX034, PRX009 or imiquimod. Representative cytokine response profiles demonstrate differentiated pharmacology among TLR7 agonists that supported selection of PRX034 for clinical development. Representative soluble and transcriptional pharmacodynamic biomarkers demonstrating coordinated activation of an interferon-biased response during intermittent administration of PRTX007 in healthy volunteers (Study PRTX007-002)Abstract 138 Figure 2Healthy volunteers received oral PRTX007 using a weekly 3-days-on/4-days-off schedule. title: Hepatitis aguda de patrón hepatocelular asociada a infección primaria por virus de Epstein-Barr en una mujer inmunocompetente: reporte de caso
abstract: Introducción: La afectación hepática asociada a infección aguda por virus de Epstein-Barr es frecuente, aunque generalmente cursa con elevaciones leves y autolimitadas de las aminotransferasas. La hepatitis aguda clínicamente manifiesta como forma predominante de presentación constituye una manifestación menos habitual y puede representar un reto diagnóstico. Presentación del caso: Mujer de 25 años, inmunocompetente, con antecedente de hipotiroidismo primario y síndrome ovárico metabólico poliendócrino, quien presentó síndrome febril de 12 días de evolución asociado a dolor en hipocondrio derecho. Durante su evaluación se documentó leucocitosis con linfocitosis absoluta marcada, hepatoesplenomegalia y elevación significativa de aminotransferasas con patrón predominantemente hepatocelular (AST 417 U/L, ALT 833 U/L), bilirrubinas normales y función sintética hepática conservada. Inicialmente se consideraron diversas etiologías infecciosas y hepatobiliares; sin embargo, la presencia de hepatoesplenomegalia y linfocitosis orientó la sospecha hacia infección por VEB. Los estudios serológicos mostraron anticuerpos anti-VCA IgM y anti-VCA IgG positivos, con EBNA negativo, compatibles con infección aguda por VEB. Se descartaron infección por VIH, hepatitis B y hepatitis C. La tomografía abdominal evidenció hepatomegalia y esplenomegalia sin datos de obstrucción biliar. La paciente recibió tratamiento de soporte, con evolución clínica favorable y descenso progresivo de las alteraciones hematológicas y bioquímicas durante la hospitalización y el seguimiento ambulatorio. Conclusiones: La infección aguda por VEB debe considerarse dentro del diagnóstico diferencial de pacientes jóvenes con síndrome febril, hepatoesplenomegalia, linfocitosis y hepatitis aguda, incluso en ausencia de las manifestaciones clásicas de mononucleosis infecciosa. El reconocimiento oportuno de esta entidad puede contribuir a orientar adecuadamente el abordaje diagnóstico diferencial.

Presentación del caso: Mujer de 25 años, inmunocompetente, con antecedente de hipotiroidismo primario y síndrome ovárico metabólico poliendócrino, quien presentó síndrome febril de 12 días de evolución asociado a dolor en hipocondrio derecho. Durante su evaluación se documentó leucocitosis con linfocitosis absoluta marcada, hepatoesplenomegalia y elevación significativa de aminotransferasas con patrón predominantemente hepatocelular (AST 417 U/L, ALT 833 U/L), bilirrubinas normales y función sintética hepática conservada. Inicialmente se consideraron diversas etiologías infecciosas y hepatobiliares; sin embargo, la presencia de hepatoesplenomegalia y linfocitosis orientó la sospecha hacia infección por VEB. Los estudios serológicos mostraron anticuerpos anti-VCA IgM y anti-VCA IgG positivos, con EBNA negativo, compatibles con infección aguda por VEB. Se descartaron infección por VIH, hepatitis B y hepatitis C. La tomografía abdominal evidenció hepatomegalia y esplenomegalia sin datos de obstrucción biliar. La paciente recibió tratamiento de soporte, con evolución clínica favorable y descenso progresivo de las alteraciones hematológicas y bioquímicas durante la hospitalización y el seguimiento ambulatorio. Conclusiones: La infección aguda por VEB debe considerarse dentro del diagnóstico diferencial de pacientes jóvenes con síndrome febril, hepatoesplenomegalia, linfocitosis y hepatitis aguda, incluso en ausencia de las manifestaciones clásicas de mononucleosis infecciosa. El reconocimiento oportuno de esta entidad puede contribuir a orientar adecuadamente el abordaje diagnóstico diferencial.

title: YM-53601 Suppresses Hepatitis E Virus Infection in Cell Culture and Supports the Role of FDFT1-Dependent Cholesterol Homeostasis in the HEV Life Cycle
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a major cause of acute hepatitis worldwide and can cause chronic infection in immunocompromised individuals. Ribavirin is used off-label for chronic hepatitis E, but its limitations highlight the need for alternative antiviral therapies. We screened 327 compounds from an anti-hepatitis C virus (anti-HCV) compound library using three distinct HEV reporter systems and identified YM-53601, an inhibitor of farnesyl-diphosphate farnesyltransferase 1 (FDFT1; squalene synthase), as a compound with marked anti-HEV activity. YM-53601 showed marked suppression of HEV propagation in cell culture models of acute and chronic infection. Combination with ribavirin showed an additive antiviral interaction and was associated with sustained viral suppression during prolonged culture. Time-of-addition analysis indicated that YM-53601 acts predominantly at an early post-attachment step associated with HEV internalization. TAK-475, another FDFT1 inhibitor, reproduced this early-step antiviral phenotype, whereas small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated FDFT1 depletion suppressed HEV propagation and additionally impaired HEV RNA replication. YM-53601 and TAK-475 markedly reduced the methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD)-extractable free cholesterol fraction, used here as an operational measure of readily accessible cellular cholesterol, whereas FDFT1 depletion produced a greater reduction in residual intracellular free cholesterol. Furthermore, cholesterol supplementation partially restored early cell-associated HEV RNA levels following YM-53601 or TAK-475 treatment and HEV RNA replication-associated reporter activity following FDFT1 knockdown. Together, these findings suggest that FDFT1-dependent cholesterol homeostasis contributes to multiple stages of HEV infection. Pharmacological modulation of this pathway therefore warrants further investigation as a potential host-directed therapeutic strategy against HEV infection.

title: Inarigivir exhibits RIG-I-independent antiviral activity against HBV DNA replication in vitro by inhibiting viral polymerase activity
abstract: Inarigivir (SB 9200) is a linear dinucleotide antiviral drug designed to act as a RIG-I agonist, activating cellular innate immune responses. Clinical trials in hepatitis C virus (HCV) patients have confirmed the innate immune-activating antiviral activity of Inarigivir. In hepatitis B virus (HBV) patients, clinical trials using Inarigivir have demonstrated significant reductions in HBV DNA and RNA levels, although heterogeneous drug-induced liver injury has been observed at higher doses. To further explore Inarigivir's mechanism of action against HBV, we characterized its antiviral effect in various hepatocyte-derived cell lines, including transiently transfected HepG2 and Huh7 cells, inducible HBV stable cell lines HepAD38 and HepDES19, and HBV-infected human hepatocytes. Our results show that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA replication in a dose-dependent manner without affecting HBV RNA levels or pgRNA encapsidation. HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays revealed that Inarigivir does not affect viral polymerase binding to pgRNA, while the in vitro endogenous polymerase reaction (EPR) assays demonstrated that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid. Additionally, we provided several lines of evidence indicating that Inarigivir's antiviral effect is independent of the RIG-I signalling pathway in hepatocyte-derived cells. Taken together, our study demonstrates a RIG-I-independent antiviral mechanism of Inarigivir by inhibiting HBV DNA replication as a dinucleosidic non-chain-terminating reverse transcriptase inhibitor.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of action of Inarigivir against hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA replication, building on its established antiviral activity against hepatitis C virus (HCV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized Inarigivir's antiviral effect in hepatocyte-derived cell lines, including transiently transfected HepG2 and Huh7 cells, inducible HBV stable cell lines HepAD38 and HepDES19, and HBV-infected human hepatocytes.
analysis.methods: HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays and in vitro endogenous polymerase reaction (EPR) assays were used to assess the effect of Inarigivir on viral polymerase binding to pgRNA and DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid.
analysis.main_results: Inarigivir inhibited HBV DNA replication in a dose-dependent manner without affecting HBV RNA levels or pgRNA encapsidation. HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays revealed no effect on viral polymerase binding to pgRNA, while EPR assays demonstrated inhibition of HBV DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Inarigivir's antiviral effect against HBV is independent of the RIG-I signalling pathway, highlighting a novel mechanism of action as a dinucleosidic non-chain-terminating reverse transcriptase inhibitor.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the development of new therapeutic strategies for HBV infection, particularly for targeting DNA replication without relying on innate immune pathways.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro analyses, and the evidence is based on cell line models, which may not fully represent human liver physiology. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of clinical trial data on the mechanism of action.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanism of action of Inarigivir against HBV DNA replication, building on its known antiviral activity against HCV. Using hepatocyte-derived cell lines, the research demonstrates that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA synthesis without affecting RNA levels or polymerase binding to pgRNA. The findings suggest a RIG-I-independent antiviral mechanism, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic agent for HBV. However, the study is limited to in vitro analyses, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of clinical data on this mechanism. The results may inform future research on HBV treatment strategies that target DNA replication directly.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of action of Inarigivir against hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA replication, building on its established antiviral activity against hepatitis C virus (HCV).
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study characterized Inarigivir's antiviral effect in hepatocyte-derived cell lines, including transiently transfected HepG2 and Huh7 cells, inducible HBV stable cell lines HepAD38 and HepDES19, and HBV-infected human hepatocytes.
analysis_en.methods: HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays and in vitro endogenous polymerase reaction (EPR) assays were used to assess the effect of Inarigivir on viral polymerase binding to pgRNA and DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid.
analysis_en.main_results: Inarigivir inhibited HBV DNA replication in a dose-dependent manner without affecting HBV RNA levels or pgRNA encapsidation. HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays revealed no effect on viral polymerase binding to pgRNA, while EPR assays demonstrated inhibition of HBV DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Inarigivir's antiviral effect against HBV is independent of the RIG-I signalling pathway, highlighting a novel mechanism of action as a dinucleosidic non-chain-terminating reverse transcriptase inhibitor.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the development of new therapeutic strategies for HBV infection, particularly for targeting DNA replication without relying on innate immune pathways.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro analyses, and the evidence is based on cell line models, which may not fully represent human liver physiology. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of clinical trial data on the mechanism of action.

title_zh: Inarigivir 通过抑制病毒聚合酶活性,在体外表现出不依赖于 RIG-I 的 抗病毒药物 抗 HBV DNA 复制的活性
source_body_en: Inarigivir (SB 9200) is a linear dinucleotide antiviral drug designed to act as a RIG-I agonist, activating cellular innate immune responses. Clinical trials in hepatitis C virus (HCV) patients have confirmed the innate immune-activating antiviral activity of Inarigivir. In hepatitis B virus (HBV) patients, clinical trials using Inarigivir have demonstrated significant reductions in HBV DNA and RNA levels, although heterogeneous drug-induced liver injury has been observed at higher doses. To further explore Inarigivir's mechanism of action against HBV, we characterized its antiviral effect in various hepatocyte-derived cell lines, including transiently transfected HepG2 and Huh7 cells, inducible HBV stable cell lines HepAD38 and HepDES19, and HBV-infected human hepatocytes. Our results show that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA replication in a dose-dependent manner without affecting HBV RNA levels or pgRNA encapsidation. HBV RNA immunoprecipitation assays revealed that Inarigivir does not affect viral polymerase binding to pgRNA, while the in vitro endogenous polymerase reaction (EPR) assays demonstrated that Inarigivir inhibits HBV DNA synthesis catalyzed by polymerase within the capsid. Additionally, we provided several lines of evidence indicating that Inarigivir's antiviral effect is independent of the RIG-I signalling pathway in hepatocyte-derived cells. Taken together, our study demonstrates a RIG-I-independent antiviral mechanism of Inarigivir by inhibiting HBV DNA replication as a dinucleosidic non-chain-terminating reverse transcriptase inhibitor.
abstract_zh: Inarigivir (SB 9200) 是一种线性二核苷酸 免疫应答 药物,设计用作 RIG-I 激动剂,激活细胞固有的 免疫应答。丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 患者的临床试验已证实 Inarigivir 具有先天免疫激活 抗病毒药物 活性。在 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 患者中,使用 Inarigivir 的临床试验已证明 HBV DNA 和 RNA 水平显着降低,尽管在较高剂量下观察到异质性药物引起的肝损伤。为了进一步探讨 Inarigivir 抗 HBV 的作用机制,我们表征了其 抗病毒药物 在各种肝细胞来源的细胞系中的作用,包括瞬时转染的 HepG2 和 Huh7 细胞、诱导型 HBV 稳定细胞系 HepAD38 和 HepDES19 以及 HBV 感染的人肝细胞。我们的结果表明,Inarigivir 以剂量依赖性方式抑制 HBV DNA 复制,而不影响 HBV RNA 水平或 pgRNA 衣壳化。HBV RNA 免疫沉淀试验显示 Inarigivir 不影响病毒聚合酶与 pgRNA 的结合,而体外内源聚合酶反应 (EPR) 试验表明 Inarigivir 抑制衣壳内聚合酶催化的 HBV DNA 合成。此外,我们提供了几条证据,表明 Inarigivir 的 抗病毒药物 作用独立于肝细胞衍生细胞中的 RIG-I 信号通路。综上所述,我们的研究证明了 Inarigivir 作为双核苷非链终止逆转录酶抑制剂抑制 HBV DNA 复制,具有独立于 RIG-I 的 抗病毒药物 机制。

title: Environmental Mercury and Persistent Organic Pollutants as Key Drivers of Fecal‐Oral Viral Hepatitis: A Time‐Series and Machine Learning Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV) are both acutely transmitted via the fecal-oral route and pose a significant global burden of infection. Existing disease predictions often do not account for environmental chemical pollutants, and there is insufficient epidemiological evidence linking mercury and persistent organic pollutants (POPs) to hepatitis incidence and mortality. Methods This study utilized hepatitis surveillance data from China between 2005 and 2020 along with pollutant emission data from the EDGAR database. A SARIMA model was employed for univariate time series forecasting, combined with a BP neural network for multivariate predictions. Key toxic factors were identified using LASSO regression, and WQS regression was applied to analyze mixed exposure effects stratified by age. Furthermore, a random forest model was used to explore sensitive factors and interactions during different dominant periods of hepatitis epidemics. Results The SARIMA monthly model demonstrated superior predictive performance for HAV and HEV incidence, while the quarterly model was found to be more suitable for mortality rate predictions; overall, the predictive performance for HAV was slightly better than that for HEV. Gas-phase oxidized mercury (GOM), particulate-bound mercury (PBM), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) were identified as core influencing factors. There was significant heterogeneity in key toxicants and risk effects across different age groups, with those aged 60 and above being more sensitive to particulate-bound mercury exposure. The shift in dominant hepatitis epidemic types significantly altered environmental driving factors: the HAV-dominant period was characterized mainly by GOM, PCB, and HCB, while the HEV-dominant period was characterized by GEM, PCDD/F, and HCB. The dual-dominant period exhibited the most pronounced features of co-exposure to multiple toxicants and yielded the best model fitting results. Conclusions Environmental mercury and POPs are significantly associated with the risk of HAV and HEV infections, with notable age differences and heterogeneous effects during different epidemic periods. Integrating environmental indicators into machine learning and time series models can effectively enhance the predictive accuracy of hepatitis incidence and mortality rates. The findings provide a scientific basis for environmental health risk prevention and targeted interventions for hepatitis across different populations and stages.

title: 390 BRII-5395, an HBV antigen–targeted LNP-mRNA vaccine, induces potent antitumor immunity alone and in combination with anti–PD-1 in a murine tumor model
abstract: Background HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health burden, with limited therapeutic options for advanced disease. The recent clinical success of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA platforms in infectious disease and oncology has accelerated interest in LNP-based delivery as a safe and effective modality for genomic medicine. BRII-5395 is an LNP-encapsulated mRNA vaccine encoding HBV structural antigens and is designed to induce antitumor immunity through robust HBV antigen–specific B- and T-cell responses. These responses may be further augmented by checkpoint blockade. Here, we evaluated the antitumor activity of BRII-5395 alone and in combination with PD-1 blockade in a syngeneic HBsAg-expressing murine tumor model.Methods C57BL/6 mice were engrafted with the B16F10-LHB melanoma cell line stably expressing HBsAg. Animals were assigned to 4 treatment groups (5–8 mice/group): BRII-5395 (3 weekly intramuscular doses beginning day 1), anti–PD-1 antibody (6 intraperitoneal doses every 3 days beginning day 8), BRII-5395 plus anti–PD-1, or empty LNP control. Tumor volume and survival were monitored through day 40 to evaluate the activity of preventing tumor growth. On day 40, approximately 1 month after final vaccination, surviving mice were rechallenged with fresh B16F10-LHB tumor cells to further evaluate the durability of antitumor immunity. HBV-specific T-cell responses in the spleen at termination were evaluated by ICS and ELISpot.Results BRII-5395 monotherapy markedly delayed tumor progression and achieved complete tumor suppression in 5/8 mice; rapid tumor growth was observed in the control animals. Combination therapy with BRII-5395 plus anti–PD-1 completely suppressed tumor growth, with 8/8 mice achieving complete tumor regression and remaining tumor-free. All mice treated with BRII-5395, either alone or in combination with anti–PD-1, survived beyond day 40, whereas all mice in the control group succumbed to tumor burden by this time point. Following rechallenge on day 40 with B16F10-LHB cells, tumor-free survivors did not develop recurrent tumors, indicating durable and functional tumor-specific CD8 + memory T-cell responses. IFN-γ and TNF-α producing HBV-specific CD8+ T cells were detected with BRII-5395 treatment, with stronger responses in combination with anti-PD-1.Conclusions The HBV antigen–targeted, LNP-based mRNA vaccine BRII-5395 elicited potent antitumor immune responses and significantly inhibited growth of HBsAg-expressing tumors in mice. The addition of PD-1 checkpoint blockade further enhanced efficacy, leading to complete tumor regression, prolonged survival, and persistent immunological memory. These findings support the therapeutic potential of BRII-5395 in targeting viral tumor antigens to overcome immune resistance and sensitize HBV-related HCC to immunotherapy.Ethics Approval This nonclinical study involved animals. As requested by Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) of Vitalstar (the CRO), the study director submitted a protocol for the animal experiment described below and obtained an approval prior to start the study. The animal welfare and euthanasia were conducted according to the standard operating procedures approved by Vitalstar IACUC (Study Protocol No.: VST-SY-25120401).

title: Longitudinal fibrosis-4 monitoring: A promising approach for hepatocellular carcinoma risk stratification in treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis C
abstract: A substantial proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection remain untreated worldwide, sustaining a cumulative and age-dependent risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, particularly in resource-limited settings. Conventional risk stratification relies on baseline “snapshots” of fibrosis stage and single-time-point biomarkers, which may fail to capture the dynamic biology of fibrogenesis and carcinogenesis. In a long-term retrospective cohort of treatment-naïve patients with chronic hepatitis C virus published in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Oncology , Li et al reported that a 3-year increase in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (ΔFIB-4 ≥ 1.0) independently predicted subsequent hepatocellular carcinoma (adjusted hazard ratio approximately 2.7), with the increasing trajectory group exhibiting a high long-term cumulative incidence. These findings suggest that longitudinal biomarker trajectories may refine long-term risk stratification beyond baseline staging, although the timing and actionable thresholds require prospective validation. Biologically, progressive increases in FIB-4 may reflect ongoing extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation-driven microenvironmental shifts, and vascular alterations that promote tumor development. However, interpretation must account for age-related score drift, biological variability, and nonhepatic confounding. We propose a pragmatic framework integrating threshold-crossing and slope-based monitoring, combining serial FIB-4 with alpha-fetoprotein and key demographic modifiers. High-risk longitudinal patterns may warrant the use of confirmatory elastography and the consideration of intensified surveillance, pending prospective validation. Prospective studies are needed to standardize longitudinal cutoffs and validate clinical implementation.

title: Circulating hypermethylated RASSF1A as a possible marker of hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis C patients
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a worldwide health issue and the third most common cause of cancer-related fatalities globally. The Ras association domain family 1 isoform (RASSF1A) is a tumor suppressor gene; it plays a role in maintaining microtubule stability, cell cycle progression, and induction of apoptosis. The carcinogenic impact of methylation, an important epigenetic alteration, is well recognized in HCC. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the significance of plasma concentration of methylated RASSF1A in patients with post-hepatitis C virus (HCV) cirrhosis as a non-invasive diagnostic indicator for HCC. Methods The levels of methylated RASSF1A were measured in the plasma of 120 individuals divided into three groups (40 individuals each): HCC patients with chronic HCV infection, cirrhotic patients after hepatitis C without HCC, and a healthy control group matched for age and sex. Methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme digestion and real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction techniques were used to assess the RASSF1A expression levels. Results patients with HCC showed markedly elevated levels of circulating hypermethylated RASSF1A compared to post-hepatitis C patients and control groups. Moreover, a statistically significant association between RASSF1A and various clinico-pathological parameters was noted. The plotted receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves indicated that plasma RASSF1A significantly differentiated between HCC and cirrhotic patients. Conclusion Circulating hypermethylated RASSF1A may serve as a non-invasive diagnostic marker to differentiate HCC in post-HCV cirrhotic patients and to assess their progression.

title: Despite High Hepatitis C Virus Testing, Treatment Gaps Remain: A Study Among Syringe Services Program Participants in Massachusetts.
abstract: Background People who inject drugs are less likely to initiate hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, and less likely to achieve sustained virologic response if they do start, than the general population. The objective of this analysis was to examine whether healthcare experiences were associated with HCV testing and treatment outcomes among people who inject drugs in Massachusetts. Methods We analyzed baseline data from an HIV prevention study, which enrolled participants from two Massachusetts syringe service programs from 2020 to 2025. We assessed lifetime HCV testing and treatment outcomes, sociodemographics, substance use behaviors, and healthcare experiences (e.g., comfort with providers) and calculated bivariate associations. Results Among 185 participants (median age of 40, 43% cisgender women), 97% had ever been tested for HCV; 71% of those tested had ever received a positive test result. However, among those who tested positive, only 41% initiated treatment. Most participants reported comfort discussing their injection drug use with a provider (79%) and feeling welcome in medical clinics (75%). Cisgender men and those feeling welcome in medical clinics reported higher proportions of treatment initiation compared to their counterparts (both p Conclusions Despite pervasive testing and high treatment completion rates, treatment initiation remains suboptimal. Feeling welcome in medical clinics may be an important, modifiable indicator of HCV treatment engagement. The gap between HCV testing and treatment initiation persists. Understanding factors that shape HCV testing and treatment engagement can generate actionable insights for ongoing elimination efforts in New England.
